articles.title: This Anthony Davis Trade Idea Could Really Save Golden State Warriors
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors are, in a lot of ways, living on borrowed time.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors are, in a lot of ways, living on borrowed time.

Steve Kerr nearly called it quits this offseason. Draymond Green sounded halfway out the door at last season's trade deadline. Stephen Curry was confronting his "basketball mortality" after a recent injury—the runner's knee that cost him two months last season, not the oblique abdominal tear derailing this one.

They could have waived the white flag by now. Some will argue they should have.

Yet, somewhere in the deep recesses of their minds, there's still enough what-if hope that some basketball magic remains in front of them. What if Curry and Jimmy Butler are healthy when it matters most? What if they're already developing a third star in breakout rookie Yaxel Lendeborg?

What if the trade market happens to bear the kind of high-end talent needed to both withstand this current Curry-less, Butler-less stretch and to enjoy meaningful success upon their return? Because there might be a way to add an established elite without giving up Butler or gutting their collection of draft capital.

It all revolves around Anthony Davis, who held their attention this offseason and sounds very much ready for a scenery change now. Let's dig into all the hows and whys of finally bringing the Brow to the Bay.

As long as Golden State's goal is to become, as Curry put it , "any semblance of a threat come the end of the year," then it has to find a long-term ceiling-raiser. And probably a short-term floor-raiser, too, since this Curry-less stretch has season-spoiling potential if things get really out of hand.

Davis checks both boxes better than anyone who is both available and relatively affordable (i.e., not a total drain on the draft capital). Now, that's obviously only true if he stays healthy, but he has been healthy so far. The injury risk tied to him is factored into the acquisition cost.

The Warriors have seemingly admitted the need for a major roster upgrade. They reportedly have the appetite for a significant trade. Davis clearly qualifies as such. Even if you remove his Hall of Fame-caliber credentials out of it, just look at what he's doing now: 24.6 points, 10.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.2 blocks.

He remains a legitimate difference-maker. His plus-8.6 net differential ranks in the 78th percentile across the Association.

The 33-year-old still moves the proverbial needle in ways that directly address the Dubs' needs: size, interior defense, rebounding, support scoring, and star power. He retains "demand" around the league, per ESPN's Brian Windhorst , though potential suitors "don't want to give him a max extension."

The Warriors surely share that hesitation. If they make a trade-season splash, they'll probably look for someone who either won't cut into their post-Curry flexibility or fits Lendeborg's timeline. Davis could qualify for the former. For all the talk about a new deal, his $62.8 million player option for next season might be too tempting to pass up.

If Golden State could convince Davis to lock in for this season and next—or maybe agree to an arrangement that extends slightly beyond that—it could still have hope.

The Warriors aren't one trade away from joining the NBA's elite tier, but they could be lucky on the health front, short of putting a true scare into the teams that are. Tag a big, ole *if healthy* asterisk onto this, but a Curry-Butler-Lendeborg-Davis foursome would be legitimately ferocious come playoff time.

When Davis and the Wizards tabled extension talks before the season, it seemed both sides wanted more time to get to know each other. Those verdicts must be rendered by now, right?

While Davis still looks like a winning player, Washington obviously isn't ready to win with him. The Trae Young extension appears to be a major misfire. AJ Dybantsa is going through the growing pains encountered by most rookies. The young core is still taking shape around him.

Whatever elevation the Wizards thought was possible this season isn't happening. This is a bottom-third team by effectively all metrics, and any hope for a notable turnaround would stem from little more than glass-overflowing optimism.

Washington should get real about its situation. It brokered discounted deals for Davis and Young last season to see what impact those veterans might have on this young roster. It already has the answer.

The Wizards prematurely locked Young into their long-term plans. They should not make the same mistake with Davis.

Now, is this an overwhelming amount of assets? Not at all, but a Davis deal isn't providing that. Not with his contract uncertainty looming overhead.

This would, however, deliver immediate financial relief—Green is on an expiring contract, and Porziņģis effectively is ($3 million guaranteed for next season)—and some helpful pieces for the future. Green could offer some present-day value, too, either attracting interest on the trade market or at least imparting all kinds of defensive smarts into this young core.

Moody, 24, sits somewhere between a rotation-regular and a solid starter. The Wizards have some intriguing, young wings, but no NBA team can ever be too deep in that department. The pick swap could hold immense value since it would almost certainly come after the Warriors' Curry chapter has closed. The same might hold true for both incoming second-round picks.

As much as Washington wants to accelerate this rebuilding process, it can't ignore the obvious signs of this roster's lack of readiness. Turning Davis into flexibility and future assets would better align the organization around its new crown jewel in Dybantsa.

articles.title: Lakers Trading Cameron Carr Could Be Key to Improving Roster Around Luka Doncic amid New NBA Rumors
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have a few obvious holes on their roster and no obvious ways to patch them up.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have a few obvious holes on their roster and no obvious ways to patch them up.

Well, one obvious way, actually, but Lakers fans won't want to hear it.

With L.A. working the NBA trade market in search of, presumably, a backup center and maybe rebounding wings, it has so far found that teams "are not willing to bite" on the future second-round picks at its disposal, per Heavy.com's Sean Deveney .

Report: Lakers Could Pursue 2 Clippers 👀

First-round rookie swingman Cameron Carr, though, "would have value" if the Lakers dangled him for frontcourt reinforcements, one executive told Deveney.

For some Lakers fans, the idea of dealing Carr will be a non-starter. Or a non-starter in terms of targeting a second-teamer, at least.

Carr had lottery buzz before slipping to the 24th pick. His scouting report points to serious support-player potential: a disruptive three-and-D perimeter player with positional versatility and explosive athleticism. Bullish projections even point toward some show-and-go creation in his future.

It's almost all excitement in front of the 22-year-old. But how far into the future are the Purple and Gold planning right now? Because it certainly feels like the franchise's present should trump all else with this team tied atop the league standings with an .824 winning percentage.

The Lakers, for their part, sound ready and willing to pump resources into putting the best possible roster around Luka Dončić.

"We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see," general manager Rob Pelinka said . "We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can."

Pelinka touched on the fact that it's early and how L.A. needs to be careful about not reading too much into this start. That said, proceeding with caution shouldn't mean standing pat.

Because a lot of what we're seeing now can sustain.

Maybe Dončić doesn't flirt with a 40-point scoring average all season, but he is obviously capable of posting MVP numbers. A healthy Austin Reaves is a legitimate co-star. Walker Kessler has stabilized the starting center spot. Investments in the supporting cast should provide more dividends than they have.

And yet, backup center is a problem that isn't going away. The same almost certainly rings true for the defensive rebounding woes ( 29th in defensive rebounding percentage ). Since Carr can't directly help those issues—he's not even a rotation regular yet—the Lakers might have to sacrifice him for someone who can.

It would be painful, sure, since no one else on the roster can match his blend of youth and upside. It would be shortsighted, too, since L.A. would likely be dealing him before he logged enough minutes to drive up his trade value.

It could also be absolutely justified if it proves the most viable path toward the center depth and rebounding presence this group so clearly needs.

articles.title: Warriors' Yaxel Lendeborg Deleted Twitter from His Phone After Being 'Baited' Amid NBA Season
articles.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg needs to tune out some of the outside noise.
articles.body:
Yaxel Lendeborg needs to tune out some of the outside noise.

The Golden State Warriors rookie told reporters on Sunday that he decided to remove Twitter from his phone:

Lendeborg, 24, has been excellent in his rookie year, averaging 19.2 points, 7.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game. But he's also, very quickly, become a lightning rod for discourse, between his back-and-forths with Luka Dončić and the added pressure put on him to take on a bigger role while Steph Curry is injured.

Lendeborg has plenty on his plate, in other words. He doesn't need the added stress of navigating the trolls on social media.

articles.title: Women's basketball AP poll: South Carolina remains No. 1 as No. 7 UConn prepares for critical week
articles.summary: South Carolina and UConn will square off on Tuesday night in Connecticut in their first meeting since the Auriemma-Staley incident at the Final Four.
articles.body:
This will be a huge week for Geno Auriemma and the Huskies.

And while it is still just the first month of the season, back-to-back losses for UConn this week — something that is absolutely on the table over the Thanksgiving holiday — would put the Huskies in a position not often seen from Auriemma-led teams.

The Huskies will first go up against No. 1 South Carolina on Tuesday night. The Gamecocks, still a perfect 6-0 on the season, remained the top-ranked team in the country in the latest Associated Press poll on Monday.

Auriemma revealed on Sunday that he hasn't spoken to South Carolina coach Dawn Staley since their heated incident at the Final Four last spring. The two coaches got into a wild exchange while approaching for a postgame handshake after the Gamecocks' win, which sent them into the national title game.

"I'm not playing, so I'm just trying to coach my team because they're the ones playing," Auriemma said, via ESPN's Alexa Philippou . "And that's what people are coming to watch, I think. They're coming to watch South Carolina and Connecticut play against each other. … I don't coach against other coaches. I coach against other players.

UConn, still No. 7 in the latest poll, will then have to take on No. 5 Duke just four days later at TD Garden. The Blue Devils are also entering this week at an undefeated 6-0, though their schedule has been far less daunting than either UConn's or South Carolina's. Duke has yet to play a ranked opponent, and has won every game easily by double digits. The closest game so far was a 16-point win over Green Bay.

But that doesn't mean Duke isn't capable of beating UConn, especially a UConn team with three losses, should it not be able to get past Staley and the Gamecocks. Blue Devils star Toby Fournier is averaging 15.8 points while shooting 70% from the field, which is the fourth-best output of anyone in the country.

Michigan remained at No. 2 in Monday's poll. Louisville held at No. 3 and USC came in at No. 4. The top five was actually unchanged from last week, as nobody in that group lost once.

UConn fell first to the Wolverines in the opening week of the season, and then got blown out by the Cardinals on the road a few weeks later. If things don't go well this week, the Huskies could be a shocking 4-4 entering December. But if Auriemma can turn things around and get through the week unscathed, he will have reminded the country that his group is still very much a national title contender.

articles.title: Lakers Trading for Brook Lopez or Derrick Jones Jr. Eyed by NBA Insiders amid Clippers Rumors
articles.summary: As rumors swirl around the Los Angeles Clippers moving several of their players, a couple might not be going too far.
articles.body:
As rumors swirl around the Los Angeles Clippers moving several of their players, a couple might not be going too far.

On The Hoop Collective podcast (around the 33:55 mark), Tim McMahon said the Clippers are expected to make several of their veterans "very available" on the trade market.

"If I'm the Lakers, these are absolutely discussions I would have," McMahon said. "What are we seeing from (Brook) Lopez? Is this something we should be interested in?"

McMahon said he believed the Lakers could look at Lopez and Derrick Jones Jr. as they try to add size.

"Derrick Jones Jr. is a 3-and-D defensive wing," McMahon said. "The Lakers could really use an upgrade there.... He's right at $10 million, in that very moveable range."

The Lakers are currently tied for the best record in the NBA at 14-3.

articles.title: AP College Basketball Poll 2026 Week 4 Rankings Released with Top Risers and Fallers
articles.summary: Houston catapulted into the No. 1 spot in the newest Associated Press Top 25 poll after winning the Players Era 8 tournament.
articles.body:
Houston catapulted into the No. 1 spot in the newest Associated Press Top 25 poll after winning the Players Era 8 tournament.

The Cougars pushed around Florida, previously the top-ranked squad, in an 86-76 victory and followed that by beating Kansas 92-83. In the midst of a 6-0 start, they were all but assured of moving into the first position.

Tennessee also jumped from 14th to ninth after upsetting Michigan State 61-46, while Illinois was rewarded for a 99-78 battering of Duke with the No. 4 ranking.

Ranking Top 9 Players to Watch in MCBB 👀

The Blue Devils have now lost 14 places from their preseason ranking of No. 2. Illinois' Andrej Stojaković avenged his earlier loss to Duke as a Cal player by scoring 46 points, the most ever for a road player at Cameron Indoor Stadium.

Through six games, Duke is shooting just 28 percent from beyond the arc as a team. While that number is bound to improve, the offense just isn't clicking right now.

"We're soft," coach Jon Scheyer told reporters after the game. "That shows in the rebounding. That shows in the paint. We're bigger than they are. We gave up 20 more points, 20 more rebounds. That's going to be addressed."

Speaking of reality checks, Michigan is unranked after losing 79-73 to Villanova.

Elliot Cadeau is struggling with the bigger offensive role he's assuming after the Wolverines lost so many key players. He shot 3-of-12 against Villanova, which brought his field-goal percentage to 36.2 on the season.

Expectations in Ann Arbor were tempered given the offseason upheaval. It might already be time to recalibrate because Michigan could be in for a tougher title defense than initially feared.

Houston, on the other hand, is weathering the departures of Kingston Flemings and Emanuel Sharp just fine.

The Cougars outscored Florida 44-18 in the paint. Dedan Thomas Jr. had a game-high 30 points, and Joseph Tugler finished with a double-double (12 points and 10 rebounds).

Houston followed that with a balanced showing against Kansas. Tugler was the only starter who didn't score in double figures. Jayhawks star Tyran Stokes (22 points) showed why he's a candidate to go first overall in the 2027 NBA draft, but he couldn't overcome the Cougars' collective effort.

As consequential as last week was, this is truly where Feast Week earns its name.

UConn and Duke face off in Las Vegas on Wednesday. Arkansas heads to the Motor City to take on Michigan State on Thanksgiving. Tennessee, Miami, Texas Tech, Louisville, Alabama, St. John's and Gonzaga all compete in the Players Era 16 tournament. Arizona and BYU could wind up crossing paths in the Maui Invitational.

Make sure to keep your schedule open in the coming days.

articles.title: Men's basketball AP poll: Houston jumps to No. 1 after beating Florida, winning Players Era 8
articles.summary: The Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 5 teams from last week's poll all dropped games while Houston improved to a perfect 6-0 in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Kelvin Sampson survived a very chaotic week of college basketball.

The Houston head coach led his Cougars through the loaded Players Era 8 bracket, which included a win over the previous top-ranked team in the country, to claim an early season championship and remain a perfect 6-0 on the season.

As a result, the Cougars jumped up to No. 1 in the latest Associated Press poll on Monday. They jumped up seven spots to claim the top position, which marks their first time at No. 1 since early last season.

The Cougars absolutely dominated in Las Vegas last week. They opened the tournament with a big win over Rutgers, and followed it up by knocking off then-No. 1 Florida behind a 30-point outing from Dedan Thomas . It marked the first loss of the season for the Gators, who ended up beating West Virginia in the third-place game on Saturday. Florida dropped two spots to No. 3 in Monday's poll.

Then, on Saturday, Houston powered past Kansas for a convincing win to claim the title. The Cougars led by 20 at halftime while completely dominating the Jayhawks inside. Houston held on the rest of the way to grab the nine-point win in what could easily be a preview of another title game come Big 12 tournament time.

While Houston deserves the No. 1 ranking after its showing in Las Vegas, the Cougars were helped by several notable losses elsewhere in the country. The Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 5 teams from last week's poll all dropped games.

Michigan State fell at Tennessee in a contest in which it made only nine total field goals. That was the Spartans' fewest made field goals in a game in the past 30 seasons. They dropped nine spots to No. 11 on Monday, while Tennessee checked in at No. 9, gaining five spots.

Arizona upset UConn in a wire-to-wire contest in Tucson on Wednesday night to hand the Huskies their first loss of the season. UConn fell to No. 10 and Arizona jumped to No. 8. Both programs now sit at 4-1.

Illinois absolutely bullied Duke at Cameron Indoor last week, too, thanks to a record 46 points from Andrej Stojakovic. That marked the most points scored by an opponent on Duke's home floor in program history. Duke, now 4-2, fell out of the top-15 to No. 16 this week. The Illini, at 5-1, climbed six spots to No. 4.

The only team in last week's top five to not drop a game was Virginia. The Cavaliers are still a perfect 7-0, though they've not played a ranked opponent yet and are fresh off a 42-point win over Loyola Maryland. Virginia moved up two spots to No. 2.

Texas Tech remains a perfect 5-0 and rose four spots in the poll to No. 5. One other beneficiary this week was LSU, which, at 6-0, rose five spots and is now No. 20.

After a few calm weeks of the season, things finally heated up just in time for Feast Week — where we'll see the Maui Invitational, the Players Era 16 and a battle between Duke and UConn take over. And for now, it's Houston's time at the top.

articles.title: New WNBA Rumors Update Fever GM Search After Amber Cox Fired Following 2026 Playoff Exit
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever's search for a new general manager is continuing without a former candidate.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever's search for a new general manager is continuing without a former candidate.

According to The Athletic's Sam Amick , former Brooklyn Nets and Dallas Mavericks executive Matt Riccardi is no longer in the running.

Amick said that Riccardi is looking for a return to an NBA front office. The Fever fired general manager Amber Cox after they were eliminated in the first round of the WNBA playoffs.

Riccardi was initially named a potential candidate in Amick's reporting with Annie Costabile at The Athletic earlier in November. That story also named Sacramento Kings vice president of basketball operations and player personnel Phil Jabour and Boston Celtics vice president of team operations and organizational growth Allison Feaster as potential finalists.

The Fever have exited before the WNBA Finals in the past two seasons, which was apparently enough for the organization to move on from Cox. Longtime president Kelly Krauskopf also stepped down from her position at the end of October, right before the Fever fired Cox.

They have several players scheduled to become free agents this offseason, including star guard Kelsey Mitchell, who has indicated in previous interviews that she might look to move on.

The Athletic reported that the Fever are expected to make their GM hire within the next few weeks. Free agency begins in January.

Despite pushback from the fanbase, Fever coach Stephanie White has one year left on her contract and is expected to return. She just will have new leadership as Indiana tries to get over the postseason hump.

articles.title: 5-Star PF CJ Rosser Commits to UNC as Michael Malone Lands 2nd Top-3 Recruit of 2027 Class
articles.summary: Michael Malone is turning heads on the recruiting trail for North Carolina.
articles.body:
Michael Malone is turning heads on the recruiting trail for North Carolina.

Joe Tipton of On 3 reported Monday that power forward CJ Rosser committed to the Tar Heels over Kentucky, Arkansas, Louisville and North Carolina State, among others. According to 247Sports' composite rankings, Rosser is a 5-star prospect as well as the No. 1 power forward and the No. 2 overall player in the 2027 class.

That means Malone now has two of the top-three players in the 2027 class, per 247Sports , as third-ranked DeMarcus Henry is also going to North Carolina.

Ranking Top 9 Players to Watch in MCBB 👀

As if landing the Nos. 2 and 3 recruits in a single class isn't impressive enough, North Carolina is also listed as a school of interest for top-ranked Beckham Black on 247Sports .

Malone has wasted little time establishing himself on the recruiting trail in his first season as the head coach of the program. He is certainly a notable name from his 12 seasons as an NBA coach, 10 of which came with the Denver Nuggets.

He led the Nuggets to the 2023 championship, which clearly carries weight with recruits.

"(Malone) comes from a great background from when he was in the league and won a championship with the Denver Nuggets," he said, per Tipton. "So it's really just knowing he came from a background that I want to get to. Just knowing that, in terms of that background, he knows the ropes and knows how to get me there at a good rate and keep me there."

Rosser has the skill set to reach that level and already helped lead the United States to a gold medal at the U17 World Cup.

Adam Finkelstein of 247Sports highlighted his ability to impact the game on both ends of the floor with an offensive arsenal that includes a three-point shot and the tendency to force turnovers on the defensive end.

Rosser is also an excellent rebounder, which should help him compete for immediate playing time when he arrives at North Carolina.

The future is bright for the Tar Heels, and it got a bit brighter Monday.

articles.title: Cam Boozer Injury Update, Latest News on Grizzlies Star's Return Timeline Amid Ankle Sprain
articles.summary: Memphis Grizzlies forward Cameron Boozer underwent imaging for his right ankle injury that revealed a moderate-grade medial sprain, according to a team statement released on Monday.
articles.body:
Memphis Grizzlies forward Cameron Boozer underwent imaging for his right ankle injury that revealed a moderate-grade medial sprain, according to a team statement released on Monday.

The tests confirmed structural stability of the ankle, and the Grizzlies expect to reevaluate Boozer in "approximately four weeks."

The 19-year-old rookie sustained the ankle injury in the third quarter of the Grizzlies' 126-98 victory over the Golden State Warriors.

Boozer has averaged 16.6 points, 5.3 assists and 9.2 rebounds per game through the first 16 games of his NBA career.

Boozer injured his ankle when he landed awkwardly on a layup early in the third quarter. He played 28 minutes, but he didn't need heavy volume to put together an efficient and effective performance. He finished the game with 16 points, six rebounds and five assists while making all six of his shot attempts.

Boozer became the first teenager in NBA history to record at least 15 points, five rebounds and five assists without missing a field-goal attempt since field-goal percentage statistics were first recorded in 1956, per the NBA .

Boozer played one season for the Duke Blue Devils before he was selected with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.

The injury will interrupt what has been an impressive start to his NBA career. The 19-year-old leads the team in rebounds (147) and ranks second in points (265) behind shooting guard Ty Jerome. He currently has the fifth-best odds to win the 2027 NBA Rookie of the Year on FanDuel Sportsbook .

Boozer's early impact helped lead Memphis to one of the NBA's most impressive turnarounds this season. The Grizzlies are tied for third in the Western Conference with a 12-5 record, but they suffered a 104-95 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves in their first game without Boozer on Saturday.

articles.title: El 'Dream Team' de Obradovic amenaza al líder Valencia
articles.standfirst: Los taronjas reciben a un Panathinaikos plagado de estrellas. Revancha del brutal playoff de la pasada temporada. El segundo mejor ataque de Europa ante la tercera defensa más sólida
articles.summary: Los taronjas reciben a un Panathinaikos plagado de estrellas. Revancha del brutal playoff de la pasada temporada. El segundo mejor ataque de Europa ante la tercera defensa más sólida
articles.body: Hay partidos que valen más que una victoria. Y el que enfrentará este martes al Valencia Basket y al Panathinaikos es uno de ellos. Por la clasificación, por el potencial de las dos plantillas, por la historia reciente entre ambos y, sobre todo, por todo lo que quedó pendiente después de una de las eliminatorias de playoffs más apasionantes de los últimos años. El líder recibe al tercer clasificado en un choque con aroma a Final Four y mucho más que un triunfo en juego. El Valencia Basket, que comparte el coliderato con el Olympiacos, afronta la decimocuarta jornada con un balance de 10 victorias y tres derrotas. Enfrente estará un Panathinaikos que no le pierde la pista, con nueve triunfos y cuatro partidos perdidos. Una victoria taronja supondría un golpe sobre la mesa para consolidar su extraordinaria trayectoria y abrir brecha con uno de sus principales perseguidores. Pero los griegos llegan con argumentos de sobra para convertir la noche en una batalla de primer nivel. Y es que hay cuentas pendientes. Muchas. Ambos equipos protagonizaron la pasada temporada una serie de playoffs memorable, resuelta en cinco encuentros y con alternativas constantes. El Valencia llegó a perder los dos primeros partidos en el Roig Arena, por 67-68 y 105-107, pero fue capaz de levantarse en el OAKA, donde conquistó dos victorias consecutivas (86-89 y 87-91) para forzar el desempate. En el quinto y definitivo encuentro, ante su público, los taronjas certificaron su clasificación para la Final Four con un contundente 81-64. Una remontada de carácter que todavía está muy presente en la memoria de ambos vestuarios. Esta vez, además, el contexto es diferente. El Valencia ha convertido su baloncesto en uno de los espectáculos más atractivos de la competición. Es el segundo equipo más anotador de la Euroliga, con 94,5 puntos por encuentro, únicamente superado por el Real Madrid (95,2). Su vendaval ofensivo ya no es un asunto coyuntural. Ha arraigado en su ADN. El domingo ante el Breogán batió su récord de puntos en la ACB (129) y en las dos últimas temporadas en 38 de sus 111 partidos entre Liga y Euroliga pasó de los 100 puntos. Una barbaridad. En la competición continental también ocupa la tercera posición en valoración (105,2), domina los rebotes con 40,6 capturas por partido —15,4 de ellas ofensivas— y presume de ser el conjunto que menos balones pierde de todo el torneo. Un cóctel de velocidad, agresividad, talento y eficacia que explica su privilegiada posición en la tabla. Pero enfrente tendrá una auténtica muralla. El Panathinaikos presenta la tercera mejor defensa de la Euroliga, con apenas 77,5 puntos encajados por partido, sólo por detrás de Fenerbahce (77,3) y Partizan (77). El choque plantea, por tanto, un interesante pulso de extremos: uno de los ataques más productivos del campeonato contra una de sus defensas más fiables. ¿Impondrá el Valencia su ritmo vertiginoso o conseguirá el conjunto ateniense llevar el encuentro a un escenario de control, contacto físico y posesiones largas? Buena parte del partido se decidirá ahí. En el bando taronja, TJ Shorts se ha convertido en uno de los grandes motores del equipo. Sus 16,5 puntos, 2,1 rebotes y 5,8 asistencias por partido reflejan la dimensión de su impacto en un Valencia que ha encontrado en su velocidad y capacidad para generar ventajas una de sus principales armas. El base tendrá, además, una motivación especial: enfrente estará el equipo en el que militó la pasada campaña, el Panathinaikos, donde no disfrutó de la confianza que esperaba por parte de Ergin Ataman. Sus números entonces, 8,1 puntos y 2,9 asistencias en apenas 16 minutos de media, quedan muy lejos de su protagonismo actual. Junto a él, Nikola Mirotic (12,8 puntos y 3,2 rebotes), Armoni Brooks (14,6 y 3,5), Kameron Taylor (12 y 4,2), Neal Sako (7,3 y 6,8) y Nate Reuvers (8,4 y 2,9) completan un arsenal ofensivo con múltiples focos de peligro. El Valencia no depende de una sola estrella: tiene capacidad para hacer daño desde el perímetro, castigar cerca del aro y multiplicar sus opciones con el rebote ofensivo. Precisamente esa variedad es una de las claves de su extraordinario rendimiento. En el otro lado, el Panathinaikos tampoco anda escaso de argumentos. Kendrick Nunn, con 19,9 puntos por encuentro, es su principal referencia ofensiva y uno de los jugadores más determinantes de Europa. A su lado aparecen Mathias Lessort (11,3 puntos y 6,7 rebotes), Sylvain Francisco (13,2 y 4,5 asistencias), Nigel Hayes-Davis (11,6 y 3,6), Guerschon Yabusele (8,3 y 4,8) y Juancho Hernangómez (4,3 y 3,8). Una colección de talento, físico y experiencia que convierte al conjunto griego en un rival temible. Y si el potencial de la plantilla ya impone respeto, su apuesta para esta temporada eleva todavía más las expectativas. El Panathinaikos ha decidido que no quiere ser simplemente uno de los aspirantes al título: quiere volver a dominar Europa. Para ello ha recuperado a una figura legendaria de los banquillos continentales, Zeljko Obradovic, el entrenador más laureado de la historia de la Euroliga, con nueve títulos, cuatro de ellos conquistados precisamente al frente del conjunto ateniense. Obradovic regresa a un club al que dirigió entre 1999 y 2012 y con el que construyó una de las grandes dinastías del baloncesto europeo. Bajo su dirección llegaron cinco coronas continentales, en 2000, 2002, 2007, 2009 y 2011. El Panathinaikos quiere recuperar aquella grandeza después de haber levantado un único título de Euroliga en las últimas 15 temporadas, el conquistado en 2024. Para acompañar esa apuesta, Dimitris Giannakopoulos ha tirado de chequera. A una plantilla que ya contaba con nombres del calibre de Nunn, Lessort, Hayes-Davis, Juancho Hernangómez, Konstantinos Mitoglou, Jerian Grant y Kostas Sloukas se han sumado seis incorporaciones de primer nivel: Sylvain Francisco, Brancou Badio, Guerschon Yabusele, Isaac Bonga, Moustapha Fall y Lefteris Mantzoukas. Un auténtico órdago para construir un equipo con profundidad, músculo y talento en todas las posiciones. Xavi Albert, entrenador del Valencia, tiene máxima confianza en su equipo de cara a este reto enorme: “Está claro que el Panathinaikos es uno de los favoritos al título en Euroliga. Todos sabemos de su capacidad, de su potencia y de la plantilla que tienen. Respecto a nuestro momento, más allá de la victoria, lo mejor son las sensaciones, la confianza cuando se ve que el juego fluye, que todo el mundo se va engranando en lo que se quiere. Toda la confianza del mundo y, al mismo tiempo, con todo el respeto de saber que nos vamos a enfrentar a uno de los retos más difíciles que tiene la Euroliga”. El legendario Obradovic reconoce los problemas que le puede generar el estilo tan ofensivo del Valencia, y espera poder atajarlo: "Queremos controlar el partido. El Valencia anota mucho al contraataque, así que no debemos darles oportunidades para correr. Solo así podremos hacer un buen partido contra ellos", aseguró antes de viajar a la ciudad del Turia. Y habló también de la calidad del ex del PAO TJ Shorts: "Es un jugador importante, sin duda. Entiende el juego, pero no juega solo. Es un buen equipo". El Valencia no está dispuesto a ejercer de invitado en la fiesta de nadie. Su liderato no es fruto de la casualidad y su baloncesto ha demostrado que puede competir con cualquiera. El Roig Arena volverá a ser un factor importante en una noche en la que los taronjas buscarán confirmar que su candidatura a todo va muy en serio. Hay revancha, hay estrellas, hay dos estilos contrapuestos y hay una clasificación que puede sufrir un vuelco importante. El Valencia quiere seguir mandando. El Panathinaikos, demostrar que su ambicioso proyecto está preparado para conquistar Europa. Y entre medias, un duelo que promete emociones fuertes y que tiene todos los ingredientes para convertirse en uno de los grandes partidos de esta decimocuarta jornada.

articles.title: El niño que animaba al Pamesa y ahora defiende el liderato de la Euroliga ante Obradovic
articles.standfirst: Xavi Albert, entrenador más joven de la competición (39 años), se mide este martes al histórico técnico, el más laureado (nueve títulos) y más veterano (66)
articles.summary: Xavi Albert, entrenador más joven de la competición (39 años), se mide este martes al histórico técnico, el más laureado (nueve títulos) y más veterano (66)
articles.body: Cuando Zejko Obradovic ganó el primero de sus nueve cetros europeos, el del Partizan en 1992, Xavi Albert tenía sólo cuatro años. Esta noche, aquel crío, que ahora es el entrenador más joven de la Euroliga (39) y tiene al Valencia Basket como líder de la clasificación, se enfrenta al mítico técnico, que es el más laureado y el más veterano (66) de la competición. Llegar a dirigir al equipo de su ciudad es "un sueño que se ha convertido en realidad". Ser el mejor equipo del continente y defender la primera plaza por tercera jornada seguida era inimaginable. Albert disfruta ahora como en sus inicios en el Ros Casares o cuando fue pasando por todas las categorías del Valencia Basket o cuando fue ayudante de Chauncey Billups en una Summer League con los Blazers o cuando ganó el Eurobasket U16 de 2023. Su llegada a la élite "se fue dando de manera natural siempre teniéndolo como sueño, pero no era un objetivo en sí mismo", comentaba recientemente en un postpartido en Movistar+. Ya se hizo cargo del conjunto taronja en 2024 después de la destitución de Álex Mumbrú. Su estreno en la Euroliga fue precisamente ante Obradovic en una visita al Partizan. "Ahora cambia el poder construir todo desde el inicio y liderar desde el primer día al equipo de mi vida", explica quien antes de trabajador del club fue aficionado. En casa de su madre aún conserva una cinta VHS con cortes de la Copa del Rey de 1998 ganada por el entonces Pamesa. "La he visto más de 60 veces". Al ocupar el banquillo el pasado verano, Albert no tenía una tarea sencilla. La temporada pasada fue la más exitosa en la historia del Valencia Basket después de conseguir la Supercopa Endesa, la Liga Endesa y la primera clasificación para la Final Four de la Euroliga. Le tocaba suplir a Pedro Martínez, antiguo ídolo, y vio cómo se desmantelaba la plantilla tras las marchas de referentes como Jean Montero, Sergio De Larrea, Jaime Pradilla, Brancou Badio, Braxton Key... Si obligan a cambiar todo que nada cambie, fue la filosofía. "El estilo que vamos a proponer creo que conecta con la afición, queremos un baloncesto con dinamismo, velocidad y con un juego alegre", comentó Albert en su presentación. A semejanza de lo que se vivió con Pedro Martínez, pero incluso con un punto más de ritmo. Ahí están los récords anotadores tanto en la Liga Endesa (129) como en la Euroliga (111), establecidos esta temporada. En ambas competiciones, los taronjas son segundos en anotación: 103,7 y 94,5, respectivamente. Por supuesto, Pedro Martínez tuvo su influencia en el joven técnico, pero él bebió de muchas fuentes. Se formó viendo trabajar a Aíto García Reneses, Pablo Laso, Xavi Pascual... y hasta tuvo relación con Joe Mazzulla, entrenador de los Celtics, al que alguna vez le ha planteado cuestiones vía Whatsapp. Mentes privilegiadas de los banquillos, como a la que hoy se enfrenta. Defender el liderato de la Euroliga ante el todopoderoso Panathinaikos de Obradovic. ¡Quién se lo habría dicho!

articles.title: SEC to vote on potentially terminating LSU's membership amid legal battle, RJ Luis eligibility saga
articles.summary: SEC presidents and chancellors will meet on Dec. 3 to "deliberate LSU's ongoing membership in the conference."
articles.body:
The fight between the SEC and LSU is far from over.

The SEC announced Monday night that it filed an amended complaint and a motion for a temporary restraining order in its federal lawsuit against LSU. The conference also said that presidents and chancellors of universities in the conference will meet on Dec. 3 to "deliberate LSU's ongoing membership in the conference."

Expulsion from the conference has been something that the SEC has kept on the table throughout its legal battle. The SEC said in its lawsuit that it intends to hold a vote to consider terminating LSU's membership, via Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger .

"The lawsuit seeks to protect the conference's ability to govern itself and to enforce the rules and policies its member universities have voluntarily adopted," the league said in a statement. "The conference maintains its right to associate only with institutions that meet its established standards and expectations of membership and that demonstrate appropriate institutional control of their athletics programs. "Monday's filing advances the conference's obligations to defend its governance framework and the shared interests of its member universities."

"The lawsuit seeks to protect the conference's ability to govern itself and to enforce the rules and policies its member universities have voluntarily adopted," the league said in a statement. "The conference maintains its right to associate only with institutions that meet its established standards and expectations of membership and that demonstrate appropriate institutional control of their athletics programs.

"Monday's filing advances the conference's obligations to defend its governance framework and the shared interests of its member universities."

LSU and the SEC have been feuding for months over the eligibility of athletes who had previously signed professional contracts. LSU football coach Lane Kiffin moved to potentially add players who had signed contracts with NFL teams to his roster earlier this fall, but the three players at the center of that battle never made the Tigers' roster.

The issue started after the NCAA's five-for-five rule, which stated that players will have five seasons of eligibility moving forward. That's led to players filing lawsuits in order to gain another season of eligibility, as the five-for-five rule only starts in the high school class of 2023 and beyond. The SEC also passed a rule this past summer banning athletes who had previously signed pro contracts from playing for teams in the conference.

The fight between LSU and the SEC was renewed in recent weeks over RJ Luis Jr., a former St. John's standout who signed a two-way contract with the Utah Jazz after he went undrafted in 2025. Luis played in three preseason games with the Celtics, but received a preliminary injunction earlier this month to play for the Tigers. A judge in Louisiana ruled that the SEC and NCAA could not penalize LSU for playing Luis.

Luis then appeared in a game for the Tigers last week, and scored 11 points in their win over UL Monroe. Basketball coach Will Wade said after that game simply that everyone who had taken the court was eligible to do so.

But the next day, LSU president Wade Rousse said he instructed Wade to not play Luis moving forward . In the SEC's lawsuit, the league cited evidence that Wade supported Luis in his legal efforts to play. Luis' attorney said in a statement that LSU was threatened with expulsion from the conference again, too.

LSU is a founding member of the SEC and joined alongside 12 other universities back in 1933. While kicking LSU out of the league completely feels like it may be a drastic step, the legal battle between the institution and the conference has only escalated since it started. Neither side appears to be backing down.

articles.title: North Carolina reportedly lands 5-star forward CJ Rosser, giving Michael Malone nation's top 2 prospects in his first recruiting cycle
articles.summary: Malone's first staff hire at UNC was to lure John Calipari's recruiting coordinator from Arkansas. That hiring is paying off.
articles.body:
The results on the court in Michael Malone's first year as North Carolina's head coach have so far been mixed. But he's crushing it on the recruiting trail.

Per multiple reports i ncluding from On3's Joe Tipton , five-star forward CJ Rosser committed to North Carolina on Monday. An athletic, 6-foot-10 forward, Rosser is a two-way player and a capable 3-point shooter. He's the No. 2 prospect in the Class of 2027, according to Rivals.

Among others, North Carolina also has offers out to No. 4 overall prospect Beckham Black (point guard) and No. 16 overall prospect Nasir Anderson (point guard).

Rosser also received offers from Kansas, Kentucky, Michigan and Louisville, among others.

Malone hired John Calipari's recruiting coordinator

Malone took over at North Carolina in the offseason to replace Hubert Davis, a UNC alumnus and former player who struggled to maintain the program's lofty standards in his five years as head coach.

Malone joined North Carolina as a virtual NBA lifer and the first head coach without ties to the program since Frank McGuire took the reins in 1952. He previously coached the Denver Nuggets to eight winning seasons out of 10 and the franchise's first NBA championship in 2023.

But his arrival came with questions about his ability to adjust to college basketball after spending his previous 22 seasons coaching in the NBA. He gave himself an early leg up. Malone's first staff hire was to lure Chuck Martin away from Arkansas as his associate head coach.

Martin was John Calipari's recruiting coordinator at Arkansas and during his latter years at Kentucky in addition to working as an assistant under Calipari at Memphis. He also worked for Malone when Malone was the head coach at Manhattan from 1999-2000. The hiring is already paying dividends for Malone and North Carolina.

On the court, the Tar Heels are off to a 4-1 start without having yet played a top 25 opponent. Their loss arrived at home to unranked Georgia on Nov. 13.

They have upcoming non-conference games against Arkansas and Kentucky, among others, before getting into the heart of their ACC slate.

articles.title: The Southeastern Conference, in a New Federal Court Filing, Is Again Threatening to Kick LSU Out
articles.summary: A new court filing by the Southeastern Conference in a federal lawsuit against LSU states that conference plans to meet next week to vote on whether to expel LSU from the league it helped found.
articles.body:
A new court filing by the Southeastern Conference in a federal lawsuit against LSU states that conference plans to meet next week to vote on whether to expel LSU from the league it helped found.

The lawsuit, filed in Birmingham, Alabama, stems from LSU's recent attempts since the beginning of the fall semester to add football and basketball players who were recently under contract with NFL and NBA teams.

Although LSU and football coach Lane Kiffin decided against fielding two football players who'd won state court injunctions allowing them to play at the college level again, the Tigers' basketball team did play RJ Luis Jr. — who'd spent parts of the 2025 NBA offseason with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics — in a victory over Louisiana-Monroe last week.

"The lawsuit seeks to protect the Conference's ability to govern itself and to enforce the rules and policies its member universities have voluntarily adopted," the SEC said in a statement Monday.

"The Conference maintains its right to associate only with institutions that meet its established standards and expectations of membership and that demonstrate appropriate institutional control of their athletics programs," the statement continued, adding that the new filing "advances the Conference's obligation to defend its governance framework and the shared interests of its member universities."

Luis scored 11 points and grabbed nine rebounds in 15 minutes on the court in his only game for LSU thus far and was note made available to speak with media after the game.

LSU coach Will Wade indicated that he would continue to play Luis as long as he was eligible. But before LSU played again last weekend, LSU president Wade Rousse released a statement saying he'd instructed Wade to stop playing Luis for the time being.

A state district court judge in Baton Rouge has issued a preliminary injunction blocking the NCAA or SEC from declaring Luis ineligible or punishing LSU for playing him.

The SEC has stated that it will abide by that ruling, but only as long as it is in effect, and maintains the position that LSU is breaking SEC rules. The league also has argued that it is unclear who controls Louisiana's flagship state university because of Louisiana's Gov. Jeff Landry's instillation of new leadership at the institution — including the university president, members of the LSU Board of Supervisors and Athletic Director Verge Ausberry.

This marks the second time since September that the SEC has threatened to kick LSU out , but it remains possible, as with the first instance, that LSU will take action to appease the league before its scheduled Dec. 3 meeting.

articles.title: SEC threatens the nuclear option as LSU’s rebellion puts conference future at risk
articles.summary: The SEC filed a motion signaling a special meeting to decide on terminating LSU after Will Wade played RJ Luis despite telling Greg Sankey he wouldn't.
articles.body: The SEC’s ongoing feud with LSU now comes with a threat that would have once seemed unthinkable: kicking the Tigers out of the conference in a meeting Dec. 3. In a federal court filing Monday, the Southeastern Conference said it will hold a special meeting next month to consider whether to "terminate" LSU’s membership amid the ongoing fight involving RJ Luis and two football players. Whether conference leaders would actually take that step is another question. But after months of legal threats, courtroom showdowns and last-minute roster decisions, the SEC is putting LSU’s future on the table. LANE KIFFIN’S ROSTER FIGHT SET THE STAGE, WILL WADE JUST THREW A GRENADE IN LSU-SEC WAR WITH RJ LUIS The latest escalation follows Will Wade’s decision to play Luis against Louisiana-Monroe last week, six days after a Baton Rouge judge granted the former professional basketball player an injunction allowing him to compete. That appearance reignited a fight that began months earlier, when Lane Kiffin’s football program considered rostering two players with NFL experience in the preseason. On the eve of LSU’s season opener against Clemson, school officials ultimately decided against adding Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris to the roster, despite a judge’s order permitting them to play. By then, the dispute had already spilled into federal court. The day before that roster decision, SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey testified in the football players’ eligibility lawsuit against the conference and NCAA. That same day, the SEC filed a federal lawsuit against LSU President Wade Rousse and other university officials, including Kiffin. DEION SANDERS TO THE NFL? CRAIG CARTON EXPLAINS WHY HE CAN SAVE A FLOUNDERING NFL FRANCHISE? The conference argued that using a court order to circumvent its eligibility rules interfered with its First Amendment right to govern its membership. LSU has since asked a federal judge to dismiss the lawsuit. While both sides await a ruling, the SEC’s latest filing adds another layer to a fight that keeps finding ways to get uglier. SEC's Greg Sankey says LSU lied to him about playing RJ Luis The possibility that LSU would roster Luis was always going to create another confrontation. This is the same school that kept the SEC guessing about Wright and Harris until the final hours before football rosters were due. When Luis added the conference to his eligibility lawsuit last month, another showdown seemed inevitable. LSU LEAVES FORMER PRO-ATHLETES OFF FINAL ROSTER, ONE NIGHT BEFORE SEC TAKES LANE KIFFIN AND TIGERS TO COURT Even though a judge granted Luis an injunction to play, there was an expectation within the SEC president's circle that the Tigers would not actually put him on the court. To make matters worse, one of the attorneys representing RJ Luis, Tony Clayton, filed a motion to hold Greg Sankey in contempt of court on the same day. SEC ACCUSES LSU OF DEFYING ITS RULES AS WILL WADE’S BASKETBALL ROSTER ADDS FUEL TO A BURNING FIRE According to Greg Sankey, that expectation came from assurances by Wade and LSU athletic director Verge Ausberry. "Before Defendants rostered Mr. Luis on Nov. 17, 2026, as discussed below, LSU officials indicated to me on multiple occasions—including a text message from Defendant Ausberry to me on September 5, 2026 and a phone call between Defendant Wade and me on October 14, 2026 — that Mr. Luis would not play for LSU’s basketball team," Sankey said on Monday in a declaration filed in federal court. LSU PRESIDENT WADE ROUSSE ENDS LANE KIFFIN’S SEC SHOWDOWN, BUT THERE IS STILL RELATIONSHIPS TO MEND Then Wade sent RJ Luis into the game last Wednesday, and whatever understanding existed between LSU and the conference went out the window. It was the following day, according to multiple sources, that LSU President Wade Rousse took a phone call from Sankey to let him know the seriousness of what had just transpired the previous night and that SEC presidents were preparing to discuss how to penalize the Tigers on teleconference taking place later that afternoon. That evening, Rousse released a statement announcing that he had instructed Wade to stop playing Luis. While that might have calmed the waters for about 20 minutes, SEC presidents were furious that LSU would once again put them in a position to potentially act. Will the SEC actually kick LSU out of the conference? The prospect still seems unlikely. Expelling LSU would require a two-thirds vote (11), and scheduling a meeting to consider that option does not mean the votes are there, yet. But dismissing this as another empty threat would ignore how far the dispute has escalated. After LSU and Will Wade pulled the pin and throwing the grenade last week by playing RJ Luis, the conference is now prepared to discuss the matter further. INSIDE A LOUISIANA COURTROOM: SEC-LSU LEGAL CIRCUS PLAYED OUT LIKE A JOHN GRISHAM NOVEL IN STUNNING SHOWDOWN Also, none of the shenanigans involving LSU over the past four months happened without President Wade Rousse, and even Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry, giving the athletic department permission to test the SEC's power. "That was the final straw for SEC leaders, they were ready to penalize them (LSU) in some form or fashion," one source familiar with the discussions told OutKick last week. "You can only poke the bear so many times before they decide to pounce, and they (SEC Presidents and Chancellors) had seen enough nonsense from LSU. "Who knows if they would have actually boycotted games, or even tried. But lawyers from schools within the conference were going through their options. This whole thing is just annoying. Like, get your s— together, and I mean everyone involved." LSU’s repeated challenges to the conference have unfolded with the backing of Rousse and Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry. The school has shown a willingness to test how much authority the SEC can exercise when a judge has cleared an athlete to play. That is the heart of this fight: LSU has leaned on court orders allowing athletes to compete, while the SEC has defended its right to enforce conference eligibility rules. Playing Luis made clear that LSU was willing to push that conflict further, even with a federal lawsuit hanging over the dispute in an Alabama courtroom. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP There could also be another legal chapter. The athletes involved could pursue damages against the conference, though whether that happens remains to be seen. For now, the immediate question is how far SEC leaders are willing to go. What began as an eligibility dispute now carries consequences that reach well beyond a roster spot. The SEC has put its most drastic option on the table. Next month, we find out whether conference leaders are prepared to act on it — or whether the threat itself is the point.

articles.title: Grading Gabe Vincent’s Signing With Kings: Examining Role And Fit
articles.summary: The Sacramento Kings finalized the signing of Gabe Vincent to address their backcourt issues. But is this deal truly worth it?
articles.body:
Since Ben Simmons was sidelined for the season with an Achilles injury , the Sacramento Kings have actively been on the lookout for a viable replacement to shore up their backcourt rotation. Now, with Gabe Vincent 's signing, the Kings appear to have addressed this issue.

According to ESPN's Shams Charania , the Sacramento Kings signed former Atlanta Hawks guard Gabe Vincent to serve as a backup point guard behind Darius Acuff Jr. Considering that earlier reports even suggested that the Kings were interested in a veteran to mentor the rookie , Vincent's signing seems meaningful.

Like Simmons, Vincent has signed a one-year, non-guaranteed deal with the Kings, according to HoopsHype's Michael Scotto . Since he's already 30 and received few offers in free agency, a non-guaranteed veteran minimum deal gives the Kings considerable flexibility. But is it really a good signing?

Gabe Vincent Has The Tools To Be Reliable

One of the main factors that could make Gabe Vincent a solid signing for the Sacramento Kings is his skill set. Aside from his veteran experience, Vincent positions himself as a reliable two-way player with solid ball-handling ability and scoring upside.

On the face of it, these traits haven't really come to light over the last few seasons, primarily because the guard has found himself in odd situations with the Los Angeles Lakers and the Atlanta Hawks.

During his stint with the Purple and Gold, the guard struggled with injuries, which, in turn, prevented him from establishing any consistency. This was reflected in his performance, as he only posted 5.6 points, 1.4 assists, and 0.7 steals per game while shooting 38.1% from the field and 34.1% from three-point range during his tenure with the team.

By the 2025-26 season, Gabe Vincent had all but fallen out of the rotation. To that extent, he had even fewer opportunities to establish himself with the Hawks, earning only 13.3 minutes per game. Given the scarcity, his averages of 3.9 points, 1.6 assists, and 0.5 rebounds per game are not an accurate depiction of his ability.

In many ways, understanding Vincent's value requires one to take his performances with the Miami Heat into account, where he averaged 7.7 points, 2.3 assists, and 0.8 steals per game over four seasons. If he earns more minutes with the Kings and is given some leeway on offense, he could be impactful.

Aside from his potential to be a contributor for the Sacramento Kings, the franchise will be more intrigued by his upside as a mentor to players like Darius Acuff Jr.

The Kings' rookie has already positioned himself as the future face of the franchise . Although he had a poor start to the campaign from an efficiency perspective, Acuff Jr. has flourished offensively , averaging 25.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 7.4 assists per game while shooting 40.5% from the field and 32.9% from three-point range.

So what role does Gabe Vincent have to play here?

For starters, unlike Acuff, Vincent made his way into the NBA through the G League. After going undrafted in 2018, the guard only earned a spot on an NBA roster two years later, when the Heat signed him to a two-way contract.

These experiences could provide Acuff with valuable insight into the amount of work it takes to remain in the league. When already considering his potential to be a star, having a solid work ethic could be the difference between being elite and being just talented.

Apart from insight, Vincent's experience against different defensive schemes could also serve as a catalyst for Acuff's development. In some ways, the upside to this may be limited since Vincent often faced second-unit defenses. But when factoring in that he started for the Heat in the 2023 NBA Finals, there may be more value in this.

To be honest, there is a lot to like about this move. When examining the Sacramento Kings' point guard depth behind Darius Acuff Jr., especially in light of what it should have been with Ben Simmons in the rotation, the current lineup isn't very inspiring. Although Gabe Vincent's addition doesn't dramatically change this situation, having a veteran point guard who can stabilize the rotation can be reassuring.

From a fit perspective, Vincent brings a lot to the table. As an extremely adaptable player, the 30-year-old effectively functions as a plug-and-play piece at this point in his career. Hence, even if the Kings choose to use him as a 3-and-D role player rather than a backup playmaker, Vincent is more than capable of fulfilling his duties.

While there are many positives with this signing, assuming that Gabe Vincent's addition will magically transform the Kings into a more competitive team would be excessively optimistic. When also considering that they are sitting in last place in the West (2-14) despite their latest win , such an expectation would also be unfair.

Realistically, the only reason this signing is not graded lower is because of Gabe Vincent's contract. In previous seasons, the veteran's contract amount has often influenced how his performances have been perceived. Now that he's on a minimum deal, even matching his production from his last stint with the Lakers (4.8 PPG, 1.3 APG, 0.5 SPG) could be viewed favorably.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama missing first game of season due to back tightness, De'Aaron Fox also out vs. Kings
articles.summary: Both Spurs stars are expected to return for Wednesday's NBA Cup game against the Portland Trail Blazers.
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs were without both Victor Wembanyama and De'Aaron Fox on Monday night.

Wembanyama was ruled out of the Spurs' matchup with the Sacramento Kings due to back tightness, the team announced shortly before the game was set to tip off at the Golden 1 Center. Fox is dealing with a shin contusion, and was ruled out at the same time..

While losing two star players for any contest is undoubtedly concerning, the two injuries were described as simply "bumps and bruises" by San Antonio Express-News' Jeff McDonald . Both players are likely to return for their NBA Cup matchup against the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday, too.

The game is the first that Wembanyama has missed all season. He's averaged 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds and 23.9 blocks through the first 17 games of the season, all of which are career-highs for the 22-year-old. He's fresh off a wild 50-point outing on Saturday night , too. Wembanyama outscored the New Orleans Pelicans starters by himself in the first half before rolling to the dominant win. It was his second 50-point game already this season, following a 52-point performance against the Dallas Mavericks earlier this fall.

articles.title: Why Is Victor Wembanyama Not Playing Tonight Against Kings? Latest Intel On Spurs’ Injured Players
articles.summary: Examining why the Spurs have ruled out Victor Wembanyama and De'Aaron Fox for tonight's fixture against the Kings.
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs are severely shorthanded tonight as they have also ruled out two key players, Victor Wembanyama and De'Aaron Fox , for tonight's regular-season game against the Sacramento Kings at the Golden 1 Center.

Victor Wembanyama (back tightness) and De'Aaron Fox (Shin contusion) now join Dylan Harper , Tobias Harris , and Jayden Quaintance on the list of players sidelined with injuries. They both last played in the Spurs' 114-91 win over the Pelicans on Saturday, November 21.

"No Victor Wembanyama or De'Aaron Fox tonight in Sacramento, per source. Both are out with what can be described as bumps and bruises. Both are likely to return for Wednesday's NBA Cup game in Portland," Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reported .

Fortunately, this is not expected to be a long-term absence for Victor Wembanyama, who is among the favorites to win the Michael Jordan regular-season MVP award this season.

He is currently averaging 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 3.9 blocks per game while shooting 54.1% from the field and 31.5% from behind the three-point line.

While Wembanyama's absence will already be a major setback for the Spurs, having De'Aaron Fox join Dylan Harper on the sidelines means all the primary backcourt responsibilities, like slashing and playmaking, will now fall on Stephon Castle .

Stephon Castle will likely also shoulder a greater offensive burden, while the Spurs' supporting cast must step up to compensate for the missing production.

De'Aaron Fox is currently averaging 12.4 points, 5.8 assists, and 3.9 rebounds while shooting 47.1% from the field. As the fourth option in scoring behind Wembanyama, Castle, and Harper, his experience could have been pivotal tonight against a frustrated Kings side looking to end their losing ways.

The Kings almost beat the Lakers last week (eventually lost 104-106) and subsequently upset the Celtics 97-96 to end their losing streak in the last game. As a result, the shorthanded Spurs side may face a major hurdle tonight without their key players on the floor.

Meanwhile, Jordan McLaughlin, who was previously listed as questionable for this game, has been upgraded to available . For the Kings, the players listed out tonight are Ben Simmons (Achilles), Maxime Raynaud (Knee), Sean Pedulla (two-way), and Jonathan Modgo (two-way).

Although the Kings have struggled for consistency, their recent win over the Celtics suggests they cannot be taken lightly. It will be interesting to see if they can steal another win tonight against the significantly weakened Spurs roster.

With a potential return against the Trail Blazers on Wednesday, November 25, the Spurs will hope this is merely a precautionary absence rather than the beginning of a more concerning injury situation.

articles.title: Ty Jerome scores 29, Cam Spencer has 24 as Grizzlies hand Hornets their 5th straight loss, 117-111
articles.summary: (AP) — Ty Jerome made seven 3-pointers and finished with 29 points, and the Memphis Grizzlies handed the Charlotte Hornets their fifth straight loss, 117-111...
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — Ty Jerome made seven 3-pointers and finished with 29 points, and the Memphis Grizzlies handed the Charlotte Hornets their fifth straight loss, 117-111 on Monday night.

Cam Spencer added 24 points and Cedric Coward had 16 points and nine rebounds for the Grizzlies, who limited the Hornets to 40% shooting from the field.

Rookie Christian Anderson led the Hornets with a career-high 25 points on 6-of-8 shooting from 3-point range. Naz Reid added 24 points, Coby White scored 21 and Brandon Miller had 20 for Charlotte.

The Hornets trailed by double digits for most of the fourth quarter and attempted to make a late run, but two of White's jumpers rattled in and out. That's been a trend in recent weeks as Charlotte has struggled to make shots from the field.

Memphis had won five in a row before falling 104-95 at Minnesota on Saturday night.

Jerome, the Grizzlies' leading scorer, appeared eager to start a new winning streak, hitting big shot after big shot and waving three fingers after each of his deep jumpers. He finished 10 of 21 from the field and 7 of 12 beyond the arc.

Spencer also played with swagger, trash-talking Charlotte's Moussa Diabate after drawing a foul on a 3 and making all three free throws.

Memphis played without rookie Cameron Boozer , the third pick in the draft who's expected to miss at least a month with a sprained right ankle.

The Grizzlies were 24 of 24 from the free-throw line, with Spencer going 11 of 11.

The Hornets were hoping to change the tide as they began a four-game homestand after losing all four games on a trip that ended Friday at Atlanta.

Instead, they lost for the 11th time in 12 games.

Cavaliers: Host the Los Angeles Clippers on Wednesday night in an NBA Cup game.

Hornets: Host the Chicago Bulls on Wednesday night in an NBA Cup game.

articles.title: LeBron, 76ers' Win Streak Snapped by Blazers, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Maxey, Top Players
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers saw their five-game winning streak come to an end in Monday's 128-111 loss against the Portland Trail Blazers.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers saw their five-game winning streak come to an end in Monday's 128-111 loss against the Portland Trail Blazers.

The Sixers entered the game playing efficient and smart basketball. Their four turnovers against the Milwaukee Bucks was their lowest on record, per NBC Sports' Noah Levick . They were also averaging just 12.1 turnovers per game , the fewest in the NBA this season. Although the Sixers kept their turnovers low, they couldn't manage to slow down the Trail Blazers' offense.

The 76ers were without center Joel Embiid, who was ruled out with an illness before the game, per ESPN's Kris Rhim . That ultimately proved costly for the 76ers, who were out-rebounded 49 to 33.

Here's a look at the top performer's from both teams:

The 76ers started off hot and took a 12-4 lead with guard Tyrese Maxey and forward LeBron James draining early 3-point shots.

Sixers star LeBron James turned back the clock. The 41-year-old threw full-court outlet passes, scored on fast-break dunks and drained 80 percent of his 3-point attempts. James led the team with his season-high 23 points.

Philadelphia saw forward Jaylen Brown return after missing the previous two games with a hamstring strain. Brown put together an efficient performance, scoring 19 points on 8-of-10 shooting in the first half. He was forced out of action after picking up his fourth foul with 10:15 left in the third quarter.

James entered Monday's game making just 21.7 percent of his three-point shots. He started the game 4 for 4 from beyond the arc, including a buzzer-beater to close out the first half.

James lifted Philadelphia to a 73-71 lead in the third quarter with his fourth 3-pointer of the game, but Philadelphia wouldn't be able to hold onto the lead for much longer.

Trail Blazers center Donovan Clingan found success with Embiid out of the lineup, and he took advantage of the size mismatch for a couple of dunks — including one over James.

Portland forward Deni Avdija thrived against Philadelphia. The 76ers, who allowed Bucks guard Tyler Herro to score 50 points in their last game, gave up 31 points to Avdija alone.

"They outplayed us," 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said after the game, per 76ers reporter Derek Bodner . "I thought their energy and hustle was outstanding."

The Trail Blazers handed the Sixers their first loss in 13 days and improved to an 11-6 record.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama Injury Update, Latest on Spurs Star's Status and Earliest Return Date Possible
articles.summary: San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama missed Monday's game against the Sacramento Kings because of back tightness.
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama missed Monday's game against the Sacramento Kings because of back tightness.

Per ESPN's Anthony Slater , Wembanyama is expected to be back for Wednesday's matchup against the Portland Trail Blazers. De'Aaron Fox also missed Monday's game because of a right shin contusion, but he is expected to be back Wednesday as well.

The injury comes as Wembanyama is putting up 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 3.9 blocks per game, and the Spurs are sitting at 14-3 on the season.

Wemby 'Had to Show Off' for Selena Gomez

The 22-year-old Wembanyama is coming off the best season of his young career, putting up 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, 3.1 blocks and a steal per game on his way to becoming the NBA's first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year.

He helped lead San Antonio to its best record since 2015-16, and the Spurs won the Western Conference Finals before losing to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals.

The Spurs have every intention of getting back to the Finals this year, but their success depends almost entirely on Wembanyama staying healthy.

Wembanyama played 71 games as a rookie before missing the second half of the 2024-25 campaign after he developed deep vein thrombosis in his right shoulder. Luckily, that condition didn't follow him into the 2025-26 campaign, and he was able to play 64 games.

Wembanyama is already on his way to becoming an all-time great, and injuries are perhaps the only thing standing between him and the Hall of Fame. He'll look to bounce back from his recent soreness swiftly as he tries to lead the Spurs to more success.

articles.title: No. 8 Arizona's RJ Godfrey Still Ineligible After Judge Denies Temporary Restraining Order
articles.summary: Arizona forward RJ Godfrey suffered another setback in his ongoing bid to become eligible, leaving him unavailable for this week's Maui Invitational.
articles.body:
Arizona forward RJ Godfrey suffered another setback in his ongoing bid to become eligible, leaving him unavailable for this week's Maui Invitational.

A Pima County Superior Court judge on Monday denied a request for a temporary restraining order that would have cleared him to play in Maui. Judge Scott McDonald set a show cause hearing for Dec. 3.

Godfrey has gone through multiple ups and downs in his bid to be granted a fifth year of eligibility and now the earliest he could become eligible is for the Wildcats' Dec. 5 game against No. 13 St. John's at Madison Square Garden.

New 2027 Men's NCAA Tournament Bracket Projections 🔮

"I will be unwavering in my support of RJ," Arizona coach Tommy Lloyd said in a statement. "He has done everything in the process correctly and is as deserving to be on the court as the next player in his similar situation. There are currently 22 players on Big 12 Men's Basketball rosters who are receiving an extra year of eligibility, and 21 of them are eligible."

Godfrey thought he would be ready to join the eighth-ranked Wildcats for last week's game against No. 10 UConn last Thursday after Superior Court Judge Jeffrey Bergin granted a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction two days earlier.

Those plans changed when the NCAA said it would not comply with the order, citing his involvement in another case in Georgia. Also at issue is Godfrey's participation in an all-star game and hiring of an agent.

That led to Godfrey and his attorneys enjoining the NCAA in a lawsuit against the Arizona Board of Regents.

Godfrey was granted voluntary dismissal from the Georgia case, but Judge McDonald, who took over the case from Judge Bergin, opted to send the case to a show-cause hearing instead of granting the temporary restraining order.

Lloyd said Godfrey was paid no money for playing in the all-star game and paid back all expenses advanced by his agent prior to his recruitment and commitment to Arizona.

"Based on precedent, RJ has met all requirements to be fully reinstated by the NCAA," Lloyd said. "However, the NCAA has chosen not to acknowledge RJ's injunction and refused to look at his request for reinstatement."

A Clemson transfer, Godfrey joined the Wildcats after a judge in Georgia granted an injunction clearing him and several other athletes to play this season in the wake of the NCAA's new eligibility rules . The Georgia Court of Appeals granted the NCAA a stay, leaving his future in limbo.

Godfrey and his attorneys sued the Arizona Board of Regents on Nov. 5, seeking a permanent injunction for eligibility.

Godfrey was expected to be a key piece for Arizona coming off its first Final Four appearance in 25 years after Tobe Awaka graduated.

articles.title: Why Yaxel Lendeborg deleted his X account? Warriors star reveals surprising reason
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has deleted X from his phone. The reason came out after Sunday's win.
articles.body: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has deleted X from his phone. The reason came out after Sunday's win. Lendeborg said he was being "baited" too much. The move arrives 17 games into an NBA career off to a solid start, with Stephen Curry injured and the 24-year-old forward leading the Warriors in rebounds and ranking second in scoring at 19.2 points per game. The last six games have been tougher. Scoring has slipped to 15.3 points, Lendeborg has shot below 29 percent from three in each of them, and NBA Twitter has been quick to notice.Why did Yaxel Lendeborg delete X?Yaxel Lendeborg kept the explanation short. After Sunday's win, the rookie said he was being "baited" too much, so the app is gone.Being "baited" online usually means reading comments built to provoke a reaction. The urge to answer back, or to stew over them, is strong for any player. It is stronger for a rookie carrying the offense while shots are missing.Lendeborg came into the NBA known for showing personality on social media during college. Then Curry went down against the Houston Rockets, the offense shifted toward the rookie, and the production dipped. The troll comments picked up after poor performances, and the negativity was starting to get to the forward. Cutting off the source solves that quickly.Many stars make the same move around playoff time. Lendeborg made it 17 games into a rookie season, an early call that reflects a good read on what helps and what hurts.Lendeborg's season numbers and the veterans around the rookieThe numbers explain why the noise got loud. Lendeborg is averaging 19.2 points, 7.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists in 31.8 minutes, with 45.2 percent shooting from the field and 36.7 percent from three. Those marks look strong for a first-year player. The recent stretch looks different, since the field goal mark has fallen below 40 percent in five of the last six games.The roster makes it harder. Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody and Curry are all out, and the three rank among the team's best players. Brandin Podziemski and Lendeborg are the only players capable of creating offense, so most of that work lands on the pair.Help is close by. Few rookies have that much respected leadership around them. Draymond Green and Curry have been mentoring Lendeborg, with coach Steve Kerr and Butler also in the locker room.The Rookie of the Year race is also in play. Cameron Boozer, one of the other top candidates, is out for the next four weeks, which clears space for Lendeborg if the shots start falling again.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
