articles.title: ‘The queen of the Queen City’: Cincinnati sports world mourns Fiona the hippo
articles.summary: Fiona the hippo, who became a worldwide sensation after surviving a premature birth at the Cincinnati Zoo, died last Thursday after swallowing a knit hat tha...
articles.body:
Fiona the hippo, who became a worldwide sensation after surviving a premature birth at the Cincinnati Zoo, died last Thursday after swallowing a knit hat that landed in her enclosure. Her death has hit the city hard, and Cincinnati's sports world has been no exception.

The Bengals, Reds, and University of Cincinnati have all paid tribute to Fiona over the last few days, with Bengals star Tee Higgins even wearing her on his sweatshirt. Now, FC Cincinnati is planning one of the biggest tributes yet, with a special tifo honoring Fiona before Saturday's MLS Cup Playoffs match against Nashville SC.

Fiona was born six weeks premature at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden in January 2017, and her chances of survival were low. She beat the odds, and her fight quickly turned her into one of the most famous animals in the world. However, tragedy struck earlier this month as Fiona swallowed a hat that accidentally ended up in her habitat.

Despite multiple attempts by the zoo's veterinary staff to move it through her system, she did not recover, and the zoo announced her death on Nov. 19.

"We are in shock at the moment," Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement. "We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn't anymore."

Jenike praised the zoo staff that worked to save her.

"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Jenike said. "She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many."

The tributes to the beloved hippo started almost immediately after the zoo announced Fiona's tragic death.

The Bengals called her "the queen of the Queen City."

The Reds quickly followed with a tribute of their own.

Her death was felt inside the Bengals' locker room, too.

"Less than an hour after Fiona's death was made public, taps could be heard inside Bengals locker room," wrote Mike Petraglia , a Cincinnati sports columnist and host of the Jungle Roar podcast.

On Saturday, the University of Cincinnati's mascot held up a "We

You Fiona" sign during the Bearcats' 35-28 win over Colorado.

Then on Monday, Higgins arrived for the Bengals' game against the Washington Commanders wearing a Fiona the Hippo sweatshirt.

The Bengals also posted a simple message before kickoff: "For Fiona." Unfortunately, they fell 22-20.

FC Cincinnati has been playing for Fiona ever since. During the club's 3-1 wild-card win over Orlando City on the day of her death, defender Nick Hagglund dedicated his goal to her, shouting "that's for Fiona" and mimicking her ears on top of his head, according to ESPN .

The club then beat Nashville 1-0 on Sunday in the first game of their best-of-three series, celebrating the win "For Fiona."

On Monday, the club announced its plans for Saturday's Game 2 at TQL Stadium.

"For Fiona. Forever in our hearts," the club posted . "FC Cincinnati will honor Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo's beloved hippo who became a symbol of Cincinnati and captured hearts around the world, during the club's Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs match against Nashville SC on Saturday, Nov. 28 at TQL Stadium. Ahead of the match, FC Cincinnati supporters will unveil a special tifo honoring Fiona. The club will also make a donation for every fan in attendance at TQL Stadium to the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden in Fiona's memory."

With a win on Saturday, FC Cincinnati would advance to the Eastern Conference semifinals. Clearly, the team will have plenty of extra motivation.

articles.title: NBA power rankings: All 30 teams ranked entering Week 6
articles.summary: Ranking all 30 teams in the NBA entering the new week.
articles.body:
Week 5 of the NBA season is officially in the books, and it delivered plenty of drama. In the Eastern Conference, top contenders continued to stumble while one team held firm at the throne and a familiar favorite finally found its groove again. Out West, two powerhouses maintained their dominance at the top of the standings. Meanwhile, a major shake-up across the league has opened the door for a couple new teams to crack the top 10.

Milwaukee finally snapped its 13-game losing streak with a win against Toronto, giving the team something to build on. Tyler Herro has been one of the few bright spots, leading the Bucks in both scoring and assists. However, there isn't much reason for optimism right now. Unless something changes, it's going to be a long season in Milwaukee.

Darius Acuff has been one of the few reasons to watch Sacramento, averaging 24 points and seven assists while leading the team offensively. Unfortunately, the Kings haven't gotten much help around him, particularly from their bench. With little depth and few reliable options, Sacramento continues to struggle to find wins.

Utah briefly looked like it was turning a corner after picking up back-to-back wins against the Lakers and Clippers. However, the Jazz have since returned to their losing ways. Keyonte George continues to lead the way, while Darryn Peterson is looking more comfortable as the season progresses. There are some positives, but Utah still has a long way to go.

Brooklyn is the only team in the bottom four without a notable win, with its victories coming against fellow bottom feeders. Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. are both averaging 20 points per game and have surprisingly avoided forcing difficult shots. Still, their individual production hasn't translated into much team success.

Charlotte has completely lost its momentum, dropping five straight games and going 1-11 over its last 12. Coby White has been extremely disappointing, shooting just 23.6% from three and 36.8% from the field. Brandon Miller hasn't been much better despite leading the team in scoring, shooting 29.4% from three and 35.8% overall. The LaMelo Ball trade looks worse and worse by the week.

There have been some encouraging developments in New Orleans despite its recent struggles. Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen have both taken sophomore leaps, with Fears recording the first triple-double of his career. Saddiq Bey has also taken on an increased role as Zion Williamson continues to lead the offense. However, the Pelicans have lost 10 of their last 11 after briefly putting together a four-game winning streak.

The Clippers have started to show some signs of improvement, winning three of their last eight games. Darius Garland has been a bright spot, averaging 21.2 points and 6.6 assists on efficient shooting. Brook Lopez has also taken on an increased role at 38 years old, averaging 14.9 points and 5.2 rebounds. Los Angeles still has plenty of ground to make up, but things are beginning to look a little better.

Since Kawhi's injury, Toronto has looked like a completely different team, and not in a good way. Losing to a two-win Milwaukee team certainly didn't help. Scottie Barnes and R.J. Barrett have continued to produce, but Immanuel Quickley has been shaky. The Raptors have an opportunity to bounce back against Brooklyn on Nov. 27, but they'll need to find some consistency.

After a disastrous start that saw Chicago go 1-9 through its first 10 games, the Bulls have started to turn things around, winning four of their last seven. They've picked up some notable victories against Minnesota and Cleveland along the way. Matas Buzelis and Josh Giddey have stepped up in Wilson's absence, while Norman Powell has led the team in scoring. The Bulls are still missing Caleb Wilson, but their recent stretch has provided some optimism.

Nobody seems to know when Tyrese Haliburton will return, with three different reports offering three different timelines. In the meantime, Pascal Siakam continues to carry much of the offensive responsibility. Andrew Nembhard has also stepped up, averaging 16.1 points and 7.6 assists while trying to fill the massive hole left at point guard. Indiana has done what it can, but this roster needs help if it wants to compete.

Washington has finally found some momentum, snapping a seven-game losing streak before following it up with three straight wins. Anthony Davis has been dominant, averaging 25.1 points and 9.9 rebounds, while Kyshawn George has emerged as an unexpected contributor with 17 points per game. First overall pick AJ Dybantsa is also becoming more comfortable, averaging 16.5 points and 6.9 rebounds. Trae Young, however, has been extremely inconsistent, making it difficult for Washington to build on its recent success.

Orlando's record doesn't tell the whole story. After a poor start, the Magic have turned things around, winning five of their last seven games. Paolo Banchero remains sidelined, but Franz Wagner has played like an All-Star, averaging 24.5 points, 6.9 rebounds and 8.3 assists. It'll be interesting to see how Wagner and Banchero coexist when the latter returns, considering how much their games overlap.

Life without Stephen Curry hasn't been easy for Golden State, which went 1-5 during his absence before finally picking up a win against Boston. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has been one of the team's biggest bright spots, averaging 19.2 points and 7.4 rebounds, although he hasn't been as effective without Curry on the floor. The Warriors desperately need their superstar back if they want to remain competitive in the West.

It's strange seeing Oklahoma City this far down the rankings, but the defending contenders have struggled recently, going 4-6 over their last 10 games. Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain and Bennet Stirtz have all stepped up, but it hasn't been enough to make up for the team's missing pieces. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander continues to give everything he has, keeping games close despite the team's struggles. With Chet Holmgren and Jalen Williams sidelined, Oklahoma City is simply trying to weather the storm.

Cleveland has been one of the more disappointing teams to start the season. Donovan Mitchell and James Harden have both needed time to find their rhythm, leaving the Cavaliers searching for consistency. Second-round rookie Meleek Thomas has arguably been their best role player, providing some much-needed production. Evan Mobley is expected back soon, which should give Cleveland a significant boost.

Phoenix has completely flipped its season around after beginning the year 1-5. The Suns have won eight of their last 10 and are currently riding a four-game winning streak. Devin Booker has looked every bit like the All-Star he's been throughout his career, while Miles Bridges and Dillon Brooks have been major catalysts in the team's turnaround. Phoenix is starting to look like a team nobody will want to face.

Dallas has won three straight and is starting to look like one of the more exciting teams in the league. Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving have formed one of the NBA's most entertaining duos, combining youth and experience. In his second season, Flagg is averaging over 24 points, 6.4 assists and 6.3 rebounds, while Irving has returned from his Achilles injury to average 22 points per game. If the two continue developing their chemistry, Dallas could be a serious problem.

For much of the season, it felt like Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray were doing everything themselves in Denver. That has started to change, with Cam Johnson, Christian Braun and Aaron Gordon all stepping up to provide some much-needed support. The Nuggets have won three straight and are beginning to look more like the well-rounded team many expected them to be.

After an 0-4 start, Miami has completely turned its season around, putting together a seven-game winning streak. Giannis Antetokounmpo continues to dominate, averaging 28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds and 5.5 assists, while Bam Adebayo is adding 19.2 points and 8.2 rebounds. Davion Mitchell has also established himself as a legitimate starting point guard, averaging 17 points and 8.6 assists. Klay Thompson's career resurgence has been another major storyline in Miami's impressive turnaround.

Portland hasn't shown many signs of slowing down, continuing to establish itself as one of the league's biggest surprises. The combination of Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard has proven difficult for opposing defenses to contain, although Ja Morant's absence has certainly hurt the team. Donovan Clingan continues to make his presence felt on the glass, proving he's among the best rebounders in the league. Portland is quickly becoming a team worth taking seriously.

Detroit's early-season momentum has started to slow, with Jalen Duren's absence becoming increasingly noticeable. Cade Cunningham continues to do everything he can, averaging 24.2 points and 8.3 assists, but he needs more help around him. Back-to-back losses against Atlanta and Toronto have pushed the Pistons down the rankings. Getting Duren back will be important if Detroit wants to maintain its position among the East's top teams.

Boston's four-game losing streak might look concerning, especially considering losses to a Curry-less Golden State team and Sacramento. However, there's little reason to panic just yet. Jayson Tatum is averaging 26.4 points, 6.9 rebounds and 6.6 assists, while Paul George has played the role of his Robin. Two of the Celtics' four losses came with either Tatum or George unavailable, so a healthy roster should help Boston get back on track.

Memphis continues to find ways to win, putting together one of the more surprising starts in the league. Ty Jerome and Cedric Coward's breakouts have been instrumental in the Grizzlies' success, with both providing production beyond expectations. However, Cameron Boozer is expected to miss at least the next four weeks. It'll be interesting to see whether Memphis can maintain its momentum without one of its key contributors.

Atlanta has been rolling, winning four straight games and establishing itself as one of the East's most consistent teams. Jalen Johnson has continued his All-Star-level play from last season, while Nickeil Alexander-Walker has proven to be a tremendous addition, leading the team in scoring at 21.3 points per game. The Hawks' depth has been instrumental, with contributions coming from throughout the roster. Their team-wide defense has also been a major factor in their recent success.

The champs are back in business. New York has won five straight games and 11 of its last 14, looking more like the team many expected entering the season. Karl-Anthony Towns has been a monster on the glass, averaging nearly 14 rebounds to go along with 22 points per game. Jalen Brunson has led the offense with 26.5 points per game. The Knicks are heating up at the right time and are coming for Philadelphia.

Houston has quietly put together one of the strongest starts in the league, winning six of its last eight games. Kevin Durant continues to be Mr. Efficiency, averaging 21.6 points while providing a steady presence offensively. Alperen Sengun has also played himself into the top 10 of the MVP conversation. Meanwhile, Jabari Smith Jr. and Amen Thompson have both taken significant leaps, giving Houston even more reasons to be optimistic.

Minnesota has done an impressive job staying afloat without Anthony Edwards. LaMelo Ball has stepped up tremendously, impacting games with his scoring, playmaking, and all-around defense. Several other role players have also taken advantage of the opportunity, with Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu both averaging over 18 points per game. The Timberwolves have managed to remain among the league's best despite missing their biggest star.

Philadelphia's five-game winning streak came to an end against Portland, but there's little reason to be concerned. Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, and Joel Embiid are all averaging over 20 points per game, giving the 76ers one of the league's most dangerous offensive combinations. V.J. Edgecombe, LeBron James, Embiid, and Brown are also all contributing more than six rebounds per game. This team has found a level of cohesion that makes it look like a legitimate favorite to come out of the East.

Los Angeles continues to look like one of the most dominant teams in basketball, winning nine of its last 10 games and 11 of its last 12. Luka Doncic has been spectacular, averaging 36.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 7.7 assists while sharing the MVP frontrunner conversation with Victor Wembanyama. The Lakers' supporting cast has also stepped up, with Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler providing excellent production. Kessler, in particular, is looking like one of the best offseason additions in the league.

San Antonio has separated itself from the rest of the league, winning 9 of its last 10 games and 15 of its last 16. Even without Dylan Harper, Victor Wembanyama, and De'Aaron Fox in its most recent game against Sacramento, the Spurs found a way to get the job done. Harper is dealing with a multi-week injury, but San Antonio's depth should allow it to remain at the top. Wembanyama continues to make his case for MVP, averaging 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds, and 3.9 blocks per game. The Spurs have been the most consistent team in basketball, and for now, there's no reason to take the No. 1 spot away from them.

articles.title: Davion Mitchell opens up on why having Giannis Antetokounmpo on the team affected his rhythm initially
articles.summary: Davion Mitchell might have revealed the reason behind the Miami Heat’s 0-4 record to start the season. Touted by many as one of the teams to beat in the East...
articles.body:
Davion Mitchell might have revealed the reason behind the Miami Heat's 0-4 record to start the season.

Touted by many as one of the teams to beat in the East before the start of the season, the Miami Heat had a horrific start, which lasted for the first 6 games of the season.

Having worked their way past that, they are currently on a 7-game win streak and have a 10-6 record. However, to get to this, they had to overcome a major obstacle, which was their overreliance on Giannis Antetokounmpo.

The Greek Freak has been incredible this season, and even when the Heat were losing games, he was putting up monstrous performances.

However, when players like Mitchell, Bam Adebayo and Klay Thompson also stepped up, things just started clicking for the Heat and they started recording wins.

Davion Mitchell heaps praise on Giannis Antetokounmpo while talking about Miami Heat early season struggles

Antetokounmpo has been averaging 32.1 points, 12. 6 rebounds and 5.5 assists this season, while shooting 60.2% from the field.

These are numbers that are definitely MVP-worthy, but due to the team's record to start the season, Antetokounmpo is not on the contender's list yet.

When he joined the Heat, Antetokounmpo and Adebayo were expected to be a dominant duo, but they started out flat. However, Mitchell revealed why that happened and how the team moved on from that.

"Playing with someone great like that, everything is going to change. Especially with a guy that can do everything on the floor, who can post up, who can play point guard, who can play the pick-and-roll, who can have the ball playing the pick-and-roll; he can do everything. And sometimes, at least for me, I got stuck watching because he can do this and do everything, not realizing you don't get a rhythm like that, you don't get a rhythm just watching.

"You get a rhythm, at least swinging the ball, initiating the offence. At first, I think we had to realise that, 'Yo, for us to be good, we all got to have this rhythm.' He can still be him, the great, but we all got to figure out how we find our rhythm in the game," said Mitchell on The Road Trippin Show.

The Miami Heat are leading the league in points with 120.7 per game. This is because they are getting the best from not only Antetokounmpo but also their other stars, including Mitchell, who is averaging 17 points and 8.6 assists.

Adebayo has also stepped up significantly for the Heat. After starting the season in possibly the worst form, he has shown great resilience to step up and learn how to be effective alongside the two-time MVP. The duo became the first Heat teammates to score 35 points or more in a game since LeBron James and Dwyane Wade.

Klay Thompson also had a poor start to the season, but he has been a major factor in the offence, putting up big numbers. He is shooting 43.2% from beyond the arc on 9.3 attempts, which is the most for him since the 2022-23 season. His three-point shooting percentage has also seen a big improvement and is the highest for him since the 2017-18 season.

With all the players stepping up, things have gone well for the Heat. They have also had good production from their bench, which has led to their winning streak. Heat's next game is against the Philadelphia 76ers, who have been the best team in the East this season. If they win that matchup, the Heat could regain the trust of everyone who had them as potential contenders to go to the NBA Finals.

articles.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo makes subtle change to extend his NBA career
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo knows his physical dominance won’t last forever, and he’s already planning for when he slows down. Even with the Miami Heat sitting at...
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo knows his physical dominance won't last forever, and he's already planning for when he slows down.

Even with the Miami Heat sitting at 10–6 to start the 2026–27 season, Giannis Antetokounmpo still feels like he is finding his footing in South Beach.

Individually, the numbers are right where you would expect. He is putting up 28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds, and 5.5 assists a night on 60.2 percent shooting, improving slightly on his injury-shortened 2025–26 season in Milwaukee (27.6 points, 9.8 rebounds, and 5.4 assists across 36 games).

Still, Miami's clunky stretches and Antetokounmpo's 24.2 percent clip from beyond the arc show this pairing hasn't quite reached the level of dominance many expected when he arrived this summer.

Giannis Antetokounmpo's three-point mission

Before the season tipped off, Giannis Antetokounmpo got real about the reality of getting older in the NBA. Knowing his freak athleticism won't last forever, he explained why shooting more threes is his plan to keep his career going.

He said on the High Low podcast : "I'm playing with my superpowers right now. The superpowers one day will fade away. So I got to keep on adding things to my game.

"This year will be the three. I'll shoot more threes for sure… And hopefully that will help me play longer."

So far, Giannis Antetokounmpo's plan to stretch the floor in Miami has hit a few early bumps. He is connecting on just 24.2 percent of his threes and 64.5 percent from the line.

In Miami, he's putting up 2.2 threes a game (making 0.5 at a rough 24.2%), which is up from the 1.3 per game he took in Milwaukee last season (when he hit 33.3%). Even with that slight bump, though, nearly 88% of his shots are still coming inside the arc.

articles.title: LA Lakers now have their 2026 version of Danny Green, says James Worthy
articles.summary: The LA Lakers last won the NBA Championship in 2020, and then-owner Jeanie Buss admitted she made a mistake breaking that team up too soon. Danny Green was o...
articles.body:
The LA Lakers last won the NBA Championship in 2020, and then-owner Jeanie Buss admitted she made a mistake breaking that team up too soon.

Danny Green was one of the key role players the LA Lakers chose to part ways with after their title success. In late 2020 they traded him away to the Philadelphia 76ers.

Alex Caruso was allowed to leave a year later, and the Lakers have struggled in the years since to find reliable role players who can fit around their top stars.

Matisse Thybulle could have finally helped to solve the problem.

The former Portland Trail Blazers star has made a big early impression for the Lakers, and helped them to beat the Utah Jazz 109-94 last night.

Lakers legend James Worthy believes Thybulle has some of the same traits as Danny Green, in addition to having a connection to the now retired star.

Worthy told the Lakers' postgame show on Spectrum: "He only had two steals tonight, he created about four more.

"Talking to him, he was under the tutelage of Danny Green for a couple of years. And if you watch his game, you know definitely Danny can shoot, but Danny also has some defensive skills too.

"He's not exactly like Danny, but he's efficient like Danny. You leave him open, he'll knock that shot down; if he has to defend somebody, he'll lock him up.

"He's a versatile player, and I think he's just starting to understand where he is in the NBA and peaking at the right time. I think he's on a big upside going forward with his career at that position."

Through 18 games of the 2026–27 NBA regular season with the Los Angeles Lakers, Matisse Thybulle is averaging:

Points: 7.8 PPG (career-high scoring pace)

Steals: 2.3 SPG (ranking 2nd in the NBA)

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns for MVP? Knicks star is making case as the best player in the East
articles.summary: New York's franchise center is forcing his way into the MVP conversation.
articles.body:
It's not the point of the video, I know. The clip the New York Knicks posted late Sunday night was intended to celebrate Josh Hart producing arguably his best performance in what's been a rocky start to the season — 10 points, 11 rebounds, 10 assists and a steal, his 18th triple-double in a Knicks uniform, tied for the second-most in franchise history — in a 113-106 win over the rival Indiana Pacers at Madison Square Garden.

What you see at the start of the video, though, is a sign posted inside the Knicks' locker room highlighting the principles that head coach Mike Brown has identified as the non-negotiable foundations of New York's offense: pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass. And at the very start of the clip, before the camera pans over to Hart, there's only one Knicks player in sight: Karl-Anthony Towns.

That's kind of perfect, because nobody's exemplifying those principles better right now than the Knicks' All-Star center … and, when you really take a look at it, very, very few people in the NBA can credibly claim to be playing any better than him.

The early-season MVP conversation pretty much starts and ends with Victor Wembanyama and Luka Dončić, the scoreboard-breaking titans leading the top two squads in the Western Conference. Expand the parameters out a little bit, though, and Towns — whose contract Knicks owner James L. Dolan declined to extend before the start of the season , and man, does it sure seem like the price is going up with every passing game — is forcing his way into the tier below them .

The Knicks are, and always will be, Jalen Brunson's team. Through the first month of the 2026-27 NBA season, though — and, really, since the start of last postseason — you can make a legitimate case that Towns has been their best all-around player. And, if you're feeling spicy, maybe the best player in the entire conference.

That's debatable, of course. Reasonable people can forward a number of names: Giannis Antetokounmpo, off to a scorching start to his tenure in South Beach; Cade Cunningham, still the straw that stirs the drink in Detroit; Tyrese Maxey, who's been the best player on the conference's No. 1 seed in Philly; Jayson Tatum, who had Boston off to a roaring start before some slippage out West .

Dig into the numbers, though, and Towns — the two-way heartbeat of a team that has won 11 of its last 14 games since an 0-3 start to move into a tie for second place in the East, boasting the NBA's third-best net rating in that span — has as good a case as any of them.

Entering Tuesday's action, Towns ranks third in the NBA in ESPN's net points per 100 possessions , behind only Wembanyama and Dončić. He's fourth in win shares , behind only Wembanyama, Dončić and Houston Rockets center Alperen Şengün. He's fifth in The BBall Index's LEBRON and box plus-minus , and sixth in win shares per 48 minutes , value over replacement player , Neil Paine's wins above replacement and Mike Beuoy's win probability added . He's seventh in player efficiency rating , ninth in DARKO daily plus-minus and tied for 10th among healthy players in Jeremias Engelmann's xRAPM . Which is to say: Take your pick of impact metrics, and KAT's right near the top, rubbing shoulders with the best of the best.

Maybe you're not such a big fan of the all-in-one alphabet-soup metrics; maybe you like your numbers a little less advanced. Well, how's this:

Towns enters Wednesday's 2026 Emirates NBA Cup meeting with the rival Cleveland Cavaliers averaging 21.8 points, 13.9 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 32.6 minutes per game. That makes him one of only three players in the NBA this season averaging at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and four dimes a night, alongside Antetokounmpo and Nikola Jokić. He's hitting those numbers more efficiently than ever, too, shooting 61% on 2-pointers and 42% from long distance, scoring under 1.32 points per shot attempt with a .650 true shooting percentage (which factors in 2-point, 3-point and free-throw accuracy) — both career highs.

Scoring plus rebounding plus playmaking plus efficiency is a pretty damn good combination. Prior to this season, Stathead's database lists only two players who've ever averaged more than 20 points per game, grabbed more than 20% of available rebounds, dished assists on more than 20% of his teammates' baskets, and posted a true shooting percentage north of .600: Giannis, back in 2019-20, and Jokić, who did it in 2021-22, '22-23 and '25-26.

Those seasons resulted in two MVP trophies and two runner-up finishes. That's the company that KAT's keeping this season.

(For the record: Wemby and Giannis are also keeping that company this season . Whew.)

Much of this stellar start goes back to those five principles — pace, space, quick decisions, paint touches, crash the glass — that Brown's been hammering ever since he got to New York. Towns might not be the first person you think of when you hear the word "pace," and the Knicks probably wouldn't be the first team to come to mind: They rank dead last in the NBA in number of possessions per 48 minutes , and tied for 28th in the average length of their offensive possessions . (Much, at times, to Brown's chagrin .) But while nobody will confuse Brown's charges for the Seven Seconds or Less Suns, they do move more swiftly with the 7-footer involved: The Knicks' average offensive possession is 1.3 seconds faster with Towns on the floor than off it — the largest differential of any Knick who's played actual minutes.

"Space," obviously, is a little easier to square here. Long heralded as perhaps the sweetest-shooting big man of all time (including, um, by himself ), Towns is attempting eight 3-pointers per 100 possessions this season , the most since his last season in Minnesota and the fourth-most of his career. He boasts the third-highest average gravity of any center — an NBA Advanced Stats metric aiming to quantify "how much a player pulls defenders towards them [...] how much attention they draw compared to what the spacing on the floor predicts" — behind only Wembanyama and Joel Embiid. (Towns also outpaces both in perimeter gravity when he's off the ball , meaning he's drawing more attention than either of them when he's spaced and doesn't have possession — creating wider driving and passing lanes for his teammates to exploit.)

When Towns does have the ball, he's wasting precious little time before attacking. Among 80 players averaging at least 50 touches per game this season, Towns averages the second-fewest dribbles per touch and has the seventh-lowest average touch time , holding on to the ball for just 1.8 seconds on average, according to Second Spectrum tracking data. He's one of 12 Knicks under two seconds per touch — evidence of widespread adherence to Brown's insistence on quick decision-making.

When the big fella decides to move, he's often aimed at the lane. Despite spending a significant share of his floor time setting high ball screens, spacing the floor or facilitating from up top, Towns leads the Knicks in paint touches per game — he's 26th in the league in total paint touches — and is taking a career-high 53% of his shots at the rim this season.

He's actually driving to the cup less frequently — just 5.5 dribble-drives per game this season , down from 8.1 last season and 11.3 in 2024-25 . He's been an absolute monster on those forays to the basket, though, scoring nearly a point per drive and shooting 67% on those plays . He's finishing tough through the contact he draws in the lane, too: Nearly 35% of the shooting fouls he absorbs have ended in an and-one — also near a career-high .

Thanks partly to the pressure Towns puts on the rim himself, and partly to how his presence on the perimeter opens up the floor for his teammates, the Knicks take 34.5% of their field-goal attempts at the rim with him in the game — a near-top-five rate in the league, according to Cleaning the Glass . That rate drops to 25.8% when he's off the floor , which would sit just 26th in the NBA .

That just leaves "crash the glass" … which Towns is doing to the tune of hauling in a career-high 11.3% of available offensive rebounds . He's turning the garbage into gold, too, tied for sixth in the NBA in second-chance points per game — one big reason why New York ranks in the top five in putback scoring efficiency .

When Brown took over, he made it clear exactly what he wanted his players to do — what he believed they had to do to reach the grandest goal in the game. After achieving it, he demanded nothing less. More than any other player in orange and blue, Towns has delivered it, night after night after night.

"Ever since I got here, all I've ever said is that I want to do whatever it takes to win a title," Towns told reporters earlier this month. "You win one and, you know, this year I want to do it again. I'm always willing to do whatever it takes. I've always sacrificed for the betterment of the team."

That's the funny thing about basketball, though. Sometimes, being willing to give it up means you wind up getting it back in an even better position to do something with it.

The sacrifice-minded Towns' usage rate, average time of possession and field goal attempts per 100 possessions are all up a tick from last season. And with New York more frequently operating its offense through Towns as a playmaking hub at the top of the floor — a carryover from the success the Knicks found with those looks last postseason, which has helped unlock Brunson as an off-ball weapon and unleashed a devastating split-cut game — he's averaging 43.4 frontcourt touches per game this season, according to Second Spectrum tracking . That's the fifth-highest mark in the NBA this season, and KAT's heaviest half-court workload in five years .

Towns has been brilliant in that more central role, whether looking for his own opportunities or quarterbacking the offense to set the table for Brunson, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, Hart and the rest of the defending champs. He has notched the assist on 21.9% of his teammates' baskets during his time on the court — a significant leap from his first two seasons as a Knick, and a near-top-10 mark among power forward/center types thus far this season .

New York's live-ball turnover rate drops by eight percentage points in KAT's minutes , and its shooting efficiency improves by eight percentage points , according to PBP Stats. When he's on the floor, nearly 60% of the Knicks' 2-point field goals have come via assist — up from 50% when he's on the bench. That's the difference between top-three in the league and bottom-five .

"They've done a great job of making their offense multifaceted," Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch told reporters when the Knicks visited — and beat — Minnesota last week. "They still have Brunson doing his thing. And now KAT, playing through him — we talked about how that was something that they found last year to go to late in the season, in the playoffs. And now, the Brunson-KAT two-man game is better than it's ever been."

So, too, is Towns' work on the defensive end — so often maligned over the course of his 12-year career, but something that started to become a legitimate strength early last season, sustained at a high level through the Knicks' championship run, and has carried over to the start of this season.

As aggressively as Towns crashes the offensive glass, he has hit the boards even harder on the other end, leading the NBA in defensive rebounds and total rebounds per game. All that possession-finishing has led to him finishing all 16 games he's played this season with a double-double — the longest such streak to open a season by any Knicks player ever, and the fourth-longest season-starting streak by any player since the ABA-NBA merger, according to Justin Kubatko of Statitudes . KAT's company there, again: Jokić, Giannis … and prime Bill Walton.

Towns' defensive contributions extend beyond rebounding, though. He's become much more comfortable playing multiple defensive schemes, including more frequently playing up higher on the floor to take away ball-handlers' airspace in the pick-and-roll. He's been active and aggressive with his hands, posting the highest steal rate of his career and his highest block rate since 2021-22 — and, crucially, doing so without hacking, averaging his fewest personal fouls per 36 minutes since 2019-20 .

"KAT's got tremendous feel," Brown recently told reporters . "He's a smart, smart dude when it comes to a lot of things, but especially when it comes to the game of basketball."

And when he's sunk back into the paint in drop coverage, Towns has proved a sturdier interior deterrent than his reputation would suggest. The share of opponents' field goal attempts that come at the basket plummets with him in the game , and opponents are shooting 55.3% at the rim when he's the nearest defender, according to Second Spectrum tracking — that's 25th among 86 players who've defended at least 40 up-close attempts, and on pace to be the second-best mark of his career . All told, the Knicks are allowing just 106.3 points-per-100 in Towns' minutes — a level of defensive efficiency that would be No. 2 in the NBA, behind only his old pals in Minnesota .

So: What do you get when you combine a skeleton-key stretch big man who unlocks a championship-level offense with a defensive anchor capable of serving as the backstop of a top-five defense, all while playing major minutes at an elite level of offensive efficiency? It sure sounds like one of the best, most important — dare we say, most valuable? — players you can have in the modern NBA.

Maybe, in a world where Wemby and Luka and SGA exist, that all doesn't add up to an MVP trophy. It does, though, produce a player that's a hell of a lot closer to top-five in the world than he is to missing the All-NBA ballot — which Towns did last season ( unjustly, in my view ). And, if KAT and the Knicks can keep up the flow they've found since their slow start, it ought to produce one hell of a title defense.

articles.title: Paxton abandons multiple cases as he departs Texas attorney general’s office
articles.summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton is dropping a number of his most combative lawsuits on his way out of office, just weeks before a Democrat is set to take his place. The Lone Star State’s top lawyer is dismissing his suits against the NCAA, multiple healthcare providers, a top Islamic group and a major Democratic…
articles.body:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton is dropping a number of his most combative lawsuits on his way out of office, just weeks before a Democrat is set to take his place.

The Lone Star State’s top lawyer is dismissing his suits against the NCAA, multiple healthcare providers, a top Islamic group and a major Democratic fundraising platform — a group of high-profile cases that some had accused of being politically motivated.

Paxton was already set to leave office to pursue a bid for Senate, but it was widely expected that a Republican would take his place. Ultimately, Democrats swept every statewide office on the ballot in Texas, and the incoming Democratic attorney general, Nathan Johnson, was unlikely to pursue the cases.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

A spokesperson for Paxton did not respond to questions about why the attorney general was dropping the cases. In a statement to The Hill, Johnson praised Paxton’s decision to drop the cases.

“Irrespective of the likely political motivation behind it, I applaud the termination of these lawsuits. It marks the first tangible and important result of the election,” Johnson said.

The dropped cases include one against the NCAA , which accused the collegiate sports body of “deceptive marketing” for calling branding competitions as “women’s sports” when they could involve transgender women. Another was one against the Council on American-Islamic Relations, branding the group a terrorist organization and asking a court to ban it from Texas.

Two cases Paxton had filed against healthcare providers for mailing abortion medication are now dropped, as well as against ActBlue , the primary fundraising platform for the Democratic Party.

“The parties have agreed to dismiss both underlying actions with prejudice. No claim will remain on which the preliminary injunction could rest, and the injunction will no longer restrain ActBlue in any respect,” Paxton’s office said in a court filing.

The case against ActBlue, which had been centered around accusations of donor fraud, was officially dismissed Monday after a judge had ruled against Paxton in June, agreeing with ActBlue that Paxton had retaliated against the platform because it fundraised for Democrats, including Paxton’s opponent in the Senate race.

The embattled attorney general made a name for himself in national politics as a firebrand who advocated for major causes of the conservative legal movement.

During his time in the attorney general’s office, he sued to block certification of the 2020 election, solidifying himself as a close ally of President Trump’s. In 2022, he faced a primary challenge from then-Land Commissioner George P. Bush, former President George W. Bush’s nephew, but ultimately defeated him handily with Trump’s backing.

In 2023, Paxton was overwhelmingly impeached by the GOP-controlled Texas House, but was later acquitted in the Senate. He has been under federal investigation, though was never formally charged, and his wife filed for divorce in 2025 on “biblical grounds” after he was accused of extramarital affairs.

The attorney general announced he would not seek reelection in 2026 and instead decided to challenge Sen. John Cornyn (R), taking the incumbent to a runoff and easily unseating him with Trump’s endorsement.

Many top Republicans feared that Paxton’s scandals would put Texas, a reliably red state, in play for Democrats, especially because national Republicans had spent millions attacking him in the primary to support Cornyn.

Paxton ultimately lost to Sen.-elect James Talarico (D) by more than 12 points, an eye-popping margin for a state where no Democrat had won statewide in more than 30 years.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Injury Update, Raptors Provide Latest Return Timeline & Recovery Plans for Knee Rehab
articles.summary: The Toronto Raptors provided a hopeful update on Tuesday regarding forward Kawhi Leonard, who hasn't played since Oct. 23 due to swelling in his left knee.
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors provided a hopeful update on Tuesday regarding forward Kawhi Leonard, who hasn't played since Oct. 23 due to swelling in his left knee.

Leonard arrived in town in September for his second stint in Toronto after the Raptors acquired the seven-time All-NBA player from the Los Angeles Clippers via trade and signed him to a two-year, $115 million contract extension .

Josh Lewenberg of TSN Sports reported that Leonard is managing patellar tendinopathy ( jumper's knee ).

Leonard has dealt with numerous knee injuries in the past, including a partially torn right ACL that kept him out for the 2021-22 season , a torn right meniscus during the 2023 playoffs and right knee inflammation in 2024.

Thankfully, he hasn't dealt with right knee issues of late, and he also turned in a 65-game season in 2025-26, averaging 27.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game en route to All-NBA Second Team honors.

It appears Leonard's comeback this season is on the horizon, at least, and that's good news for the 6-11 Raptors, who have gone 4-11 after a 2-0 start with him in the lineup. They've also lost seven of their last eight games.

Toronto hopes to snap the skid Friday evening when it hosts the Brooklyn Nets.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton, Wife Jade Announce They're Expecting 1st Child in New IG Photo
articles.summary: Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton got some good family news amid his ongoing recovery from the left hamstring strain that has sidelined him since October.
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton got some good family news amid his ongoing recovery from the left hamstring strain that has sidelined him since October.

Haliburton and his wife Jade announced the upcoming birth of their first child in spring 2027 with a post on Instagram on Tuesday.

Haliburton returned this fall from the Achilles injury that sidelined him for the entirety of the 2025-26 campaign. He played just four games before he was shut down due to his latest injury.

The Pacers star recently said in a video posted to social media his goal is to return to the court "before the start of December."

He has since been assigned to the G League to ramp up in practice, and coach Rick Carlisle said Tuesday fans should "stay tuned" about the possibility of Haliburton returning Friday against the Philadelphia 76ers or Saturday at the Chicago Bulls.

articles.title: GVSU women's basketball recap: Gaytan, Lakers crank up the 'D' to beat Findlay
articles.summary: A recap of the defending NCAA champion Grand Valley State women's basketball team's latest.
articles.body:
This is a game-by-game recap for the defending NCAA Division II champion Grand Valley State women's basketball team.

GVSU faced its toughest early test of the season after Findlay's MacKenzie Shultz caught fire for 19 first-half points.

The Lakers (5-0) trailed after one quarter, 19-18, then clung to a 39-35 halftime lead then started the second half on a 7-0 run. That quickly moved to a 12-1 run as Reese Gaytan and MacKenzie Bisballe were able to put in second-chance points.

"We put Reese on Schultz, which helped. She got into her space a little more. We stepped up and competed better and didn't let them get clean looks at the basket in the second half," GVSU coach Mike Williams said. "It was good to see us step up to that challenge."

Bisballe, Gaytan and Ava Scanlon each grabbed multiple offensive rebounds during the stretch that turned into easy baskets.

Scanlon hit a long jumper at the third-quarter buzzer to put the Lakers up 62-44, a 23-9 run in the quarter.

The Oilers shot just 17% in the third quarter and went 0-for-8 from 3-point range.

Gaytan finished with 22 points, three rebounds, two assists and seven fouls drawn.

"I have been working in my shot a lot," Gaytan said. "I usually look for my teammates, but if it is there, I'll take it."

Bisballe had 17 points, 12 rebounds, including eight offensive rebounds. Scanlon had 10 points, six rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Anayya Davis dished out five assists and had two steals. Jordyn Bonnema had eight points.

"Tonight offensive rebounds were very important. If we can get those second-chance opportunities, they will just help us in the end," Bisballe said.
